title: privacy: error-body echo wider than PR-G1 — query-path + RDF-body parse errors echo caller input/loaded-RDF fragments
description:
Audit of cert-privacy (PR #236, epic sq-toze) found the privacy gap register PR-G1 understates the error-body leak surface. PR-G1 claims the UPDATE path (`update failed: {e}`, http.rs:2116) is 'the one exception' and that the leak is 'query text, not loaded RDF data' (→ Low). Independent code read of origin/worktree-agent-af186064192837d69 found additional echo sites:
- http.rs:1812  `bad_request("malformed query: {msg}")` — QUERY parse path echoes the spargebra diagnostic (caller query text). Contradicts the controls.md P-12 claim that query responses 'already use generic bodies'.
- http.rs:2293  `bad_request("malformed RDF body: {e}")` and :2302 `malformed RDF/XML body: {e}` — the GSP write-body load path echoes the RDF parser error (via Graph::load_str → parse_to_triples → e.to_string()), which for a malformed triple can embed a fragment of the LOADED RDF DATA (i.e. actual personal data) — defeating PR-G1's 'not loaded data' severity justification.
- http.rs:2738  `malformed gzip body: {e}`.
Remediation: strip/gate these diagnostics to generic bodies (parity with the query result path) OR put verbose diagnostics behind --verbose; add a regression test asserting default-mode error bodies contain no echoed query/RDF fragment. Pairs with sq-toze.32 (which is a DOC bead, not this code fix). Ref epic sq-toze, PR #236. [OPUS-4.8]
notes:
[OPUS-4.8] SECURITY: error responses leak loaded-RDF fragments to UNAUTHENTICATED callers (B3 no-auth path) — http.rs:2293/:2302, root at sparq-core/src/lib.rs:632 (Graph::load_str e.to_string()). Same root cause as ASVS-G3 error-string hygiene (sq-kfel) — fix together: sanitize/genericize error bodies so no caller input or data content is echoed. Surfaced by the Privacy cert audit (#236).
[OPUS-4.8] COMPLETE echo-site list (sanitize ALL): http.rs:1812 (query text), :2116 (UPDATE), :2293/:2302 (RDF body), :2738 (malformed gzip body), :2860 (exec error), main.rs:875-881 (persist dir.display()), root sparq-core/src/lib.rs:632 (Graph::load_str e.to_string()). Fix = generic error bodies, no caller input/data/path echoed. Pair with sq-kfel (ASVS-G3).
[OPUS-4.8] ASVS-G3 is now tracked as sq-j9zs (the earlier sq-kfel reference was a phantom ID that never persisted). Fix sq-cz89 + sq-j9zs together.
close_reason: Error-body info-leak fixed + merged in PR #241 (HTTP-boundary sanitization, detail→server log, error contract preserved).

title: sparq engine+server: persist NAMED graphs across save/open + per-graph WAL
description: PSS DEEPEST SHOWSTOPPER (gh-45). Graph::save/open serialize only the default-graph store + dict; named: Vec<(Term,Graph)> is dropped (open() always sets named: empty); mmap/out-of-core path is triple-only. PSS models EVERY resource (and every .acl) as a named graph whose IRI == resource IRI, so the entire Solid dataset shape has NO durable/out-of-core path today -> total data loss on restart. Add multi-graph durable save/open + per-graph WAL. Acceptance: a dataset of N named graphs survives save/open AND (separately) survives mmap out-of-core open. Prerequisite for PSS using sparq at all. title: mmap_corruption_oracle sweeps can OOM-abort the test binary (residual rc=101 source)
description: The corruption sweeps in crates/sparq-core/tests/mmap_corruption_oracle.rs (mmap_loader_survives_corruption_raw/_compressed, quoted_triple_wrong_kind_component_is_safe_not_panic) deliberately feed hostile varint/length bytes to Graph::open. The test's own comment notes an OOM-abort 'cannot be caught and takes the whole process down' — i.e. a corrupt length that drives a huge allocation aborts the WHOLE test binary => exit 101 with no FAILED line, and under llvm-cov no profraw => undercount. This is a SEPARATE potential trigger of the sq-x4jy symptom from the env-var race fixed in ea0ca3e. Mitigations now in place: (1) nextest per-test process isolation + --retries 2 means one aborting test no longer fails the run deterministically and self-heals; (2) sq-znld/sq-ed2i already bound most allocations. Deeper fix if it ever recurs: cap the loader's pre-allocation against the on-disk file length (reject a declared length/count that exceeds the mmap'd file size before allocating), so a hostile length is a clean Err instead of an abort. Found while fixing sq-x4jy.
notes: ROOT CAUSE of the train-blocking coverage flake (sq-x4jy): the mmap_corruption_oracle test feeds hostile lengths/varints to the on-disk-store loader; under llvm-cov instrumentation (extra memory) a hostile length triggers a huge Vec pre-allocation → OOM-abort of the test binary → its profraw is lost → sparq-core coverage drops to ~71% (vs 91%) as a valid-but-low number (and sometimes rc=101). --test-threads=1 + the re-measure backstop did NOT fix it (still failed both passes on #62). The real fix is to CAP the loader's pre-allocation by the actual on-disk file length so a hostile length can't reserve GBs (also a genuine untrusted-input DoS hardening). Fix this and the coverage flake disappears.

title: Flaky sparq-core coverage measurement — intermittently 71% vs 91% (blocks unrelated PRs)
description: The per-commit coverage ratchet intermittently measures sparq-core at ~71% (< floor 78) instead of the true ~91%, failing CI on UNRELATED (even doc-only) PRs (#30, #57). Root cause (flagged by the #29 coverage-gate agent): an llvm-cov test-binary race — a test binary (e.g. the snapshot/mmap-oracle/dict-spill binary) sometimes isn't executed/measured, dropping the %. Fix options: run the coverage test set serially (--no-parallel / --test-threads=1 under llvm-cov), pin/verify the expected test-binary set is measured (fail loudly if a binary is missing rather than silently undercounting), or split the heavy binaries. Until fixed, a re-run clears it (see scripts/coverage.sh). Worst risk: it could also MASK a real coverage regression. Relates to sq-5fd1 (coverage gate) + the #29 hardening.
notes: DIAGNOSED + FIX READY on branch ci-fix-flake-x4jy (commit ea0ca3e). ROOT CAUSE is NOT a snapshot/golden-file test — it is a process-global ENV-VAR data race in UNIT tests: sparq-core dictspill.rs (spill_config_from_env_gate_and_overrides) and sparq-server service_config.rs (3 from_sources tests) called std::env::set_var/remove_var while sibling tests + the production from_env/from_sources paths read std::env concurrently (cargo test = parallel threads). Concurrent setenv/getenv is libc UB (reallocs environ) -> can abort the whole test binary -> 'build+test' exit 101 with no FAILED line AND (under llvm-cov) no profraw -> sparq-core undercount (~71% vs 91%). The pre-existing EnvRestore guards fixed leakage but NOT the concurrent-access race. FIX: made both tests hermetic via injectable env lookups (SpillConfig::from_lookup + ServiceAllowlist::from_sources_with_env; public signatures unchanged); zero set_var/remove_var remain in the workspace. PLUS CI resilience: build+test now uses cargo-nextest --retries 2 (per-test process isolation; 'binary never executed' is deterministic; +cargo test --doc preserves doctests) and coverage.sh retries a per-crate measurement. Validated: env tests 20/20 in a parallel loop; full-workspace nextest 1493 pass/0 fail/28 skip; sparq-core coverage stable 91.28%; clippy -D warnings clean; ci.yml valid+SHA-pinned. This should CLOSE sq-x4jy on merge (root cause removed). Residual SEPARATE rc=101 source (mmap oracle OOM-abort) tracked as sq-f5jh.

title: Reject non-UTF-8 dictionary blob in mmap loader (from_utf8_unchecked soundness hole)
description: Memory-safety soundness hole at the hostile-on-disk-file boundary. Dict::open_mmap (crates/sparq-core/src/dict.rs:1272) validates only dict-meta.bin (magic/version/INLINE_BASE) but performs NO validation of the four data files (dict-terms/offs/hash/hid.bin). MappedDict::stored (dict.rs:567) reads an attacker-controlled u64 offset from dict-offs.bin and slices blob[off..]; rd_str (dict.rs:380) reads an attacker-controlled u32 length then calls std::str::from_utf8_unchecked over those bytes WITHOUT a UTF-8 check -> immediate UB (undefined behaviour) on a hostile/corrupt store whose blob contains non-UTF-8 bytes. A bad offset/length instead panics (DoS). Fix: validate dict-offs.bin length == len*8 and every offset < terms.len() at open time, and replace from_utf8_unchecked with a checked from_utf8 (or validate the whole blob is UTF-8 on load). Complements sq-ky2a (fuzzing). Identified in research/threat-model.md (T-MMAP-UB).
close_reason: Landed: from_utf8_unchecked UB + 68GB OOM-abort fixed; Dict::open_mmap fully validates at open. Corruption oracle confirms. Gated+merged.

title: SPARQL builtins STRLEN/ENCODE_FOR_URI/LANGMATCHES wrongly STR()-coerced non-string operands (FIXED)
description:
Found + FIXED during sq-6qkq (per-builtin error-path table test), branch test-builtin-errors.

DIVERGENCE (SPARQL 1.1 type-error rule): three string builtins used the lax value_str() coercion (which stringifies IRIs/numbers/booleans like STR()) where the spec requires a STRING LITERAL operand, so a type-error input wrongly produced a VALUE instead of an expression error:
  - STRLEN(<iri>)        returned the IRI's char count (e.g. 11) instead of error  [exec.rs F::StrLen, SPARQL 1.1 §17.4.3.2 — xsd:integer STRLEN(string literal)]
  - ENCODE_FOR_URI(123)  returned simple literal "123" instead of error           [exec.rs F::EncodeForUri, §17.4.3.12 — simple literal ENCODE_FOR_URI(string literal)]
  - LANGMATCHES(123,'en') returned false (a value) instead of error                 [exec.rs F::LangMatches, §17.4.3.15 — xsd:boolean langMatches(simple literal, simple literal)]

FIX: switched those three arms from value_str() to str_lit() (accepts simple/lang-tagged/xsd:string, rejects IRI/number/boolean -> Value::Error). Tagged [OPUS-4.8] in exec.rs. All 144 existing engine lib tests still pass; new builtin_error_paths table test (44 builtins x {valid,type-error,(boundary)}) is green. clippy -D warnings clean. W3C conformance data was not fetched in the worktree so the rdf-tests suite could not be re-run here — FOLLOW-UP: run scripts/fetch-conformance.sh + sparq-conformance to confirm no regression in the fn-* string-function suite.

This bead is the audit record; the fix is on branch test-builtin-errors awaiting orchestrator merge.
close_reason: Resolved: W3C SPARQL conformance re-run after the STRLEN/ENCODE_FOR_URI/LANGMATCHES strictness fix is CLEAN — 1225 pass + 4 divergence = 1229, no regression below the ratchet.

description: Multi-party computation over (federated) SPARQL with a ZK proof the result is correct AND derived from attested sources. Spec: research/mpc-zkp-research-and-architecture.md, research/mpc-m4-distributed-sig-feasibility.md. M0/M2/M3 merged.

title: ODRL recipient neq/'everyone-except' → per-session ACP noneOf exception matcher
description: A recipient constraint under neq (everyone EXCEPT one party) has no faithful single-grant ACP analogue today and stays one-shot. It COULD map to a ConditionalGrant with a noneOf exceptMatcher whose accept-set is the excluded recipient — the machinery exists (matcher_accepts/exceptMatcher) but the bridge does not emit it. Investigate emitting a public/authenticated allow + an exceptMatcher for the neq recipient. From sq-hiz4. Epic sq-3183.

title: ODRL count constraint: stateful usage-counter enforcement
description: odrl:count has no ACP analogue (ACP is stateless — no usage counter) so it stays one-shot. A faithful re-check needs persistent per-(agent,asset) usage state + atomic decrement, which is outside the stateless auth-view model. Investigate a stateful usage-accounting layer (out of scope for the triple-based auth view). From sq-hiz4. Epic sq-3183.

title: ODRL dateTime/time-window constraint: re-checked temporal ACP condition
description: odrl:dateTime time-window constraints stay one-shot in sparq-solid's odrl-bridge because ACP has no 'now' dimension (matcher accept-sets are static sets). A faithful per-session re-check would need a temporal condition (auth:notBefore/notAfter on a ConditionalGrant) evaluated against request time in AuthIndex::accessible. This is a STRICTER-only addition (a time bound can only deny, never widen), so it could be faithfully added. Investigate an opt-in temporal conditional grant. From sq-hiz4. Epic sq-3183.

title: ODRL purpose constraint: faithful re-checked enforcement (no current ACP analogue)
description: sparq-solid's odrl-bridge maps recipient/assignee constraints to a re-checked ACP auth:ConditionalGrant (agent matcher), but odrl:purpose has NO faithful stateless (agent,client) ACP analogue (a client app is not a purpose-of-use), so it stays one-shot (frozen at materialization). To re-check purpose per session would need a purpose dimension on Session + a purpose matcher in the auth view (or a DPV purpose hierarchy). Investigate adding an opt-in purpose dimension to the session/conditional-grant machinery. From sq-hiz4. Epic sq-3183.

title: CI feature-matrix + coverage: add sparq-server 'audit-log' leg (gated tests never run)
description: sparq-server's opt-in default-OFF 'audit-log' feature (CDMC CD-2 / ISO 27001 A.8.15 / EU CRA logging) has src/audit.rs (#[cfg(feature="audit-log")]) + tests/audit_log.rs (#![cfg(feature="audit-log")], 2 tokio tests for allowed/denied records + no-leak of query/token), but NOTHING in CI enables the feature: the main 'cargo nextest archive --workspace --all-targets' job has no --all-features, scripts/coverage.sh measures sparq-server with default features only, and .github/workflows/feature-matrix.yml has no audit-log leg (it does have federation-descriptors/service/time-travel/geo/test-seams). So the gated code + integration test are compiled out and the audit log can silently break. Add an audit-log feature-matrix leg (alongside the sq-wuft filtered-ann/shacl-af legs). From coverage/bench gap audit (research/coverage-bench-gap-audit.md). Refs sq-bif. [OPUS-4.8]

title: Turtle: sharded dict merge for the parallel chunked path (T4)
description: Goal: replace the serial merge_remap-in-a-loop in parse_turtle_chunked (crates/sparq-core/src/lib.rs ~:4101) with the ShardedDict + sharded_extend + finish_sharded path the N-Triples loader already uses on >=2 threads (lib.rs:1068-1148), so chunked Turtle scales past the serial-merge_remap ceiling toward the NT path's scaling. The earlier blocker (sharded interner rejected RDF 1.2 triple terms) is gone — sq-87bq made the sharded merge consolidate triple terms (lib.rs:3634-3641), so Turtle is now eligible. Crate: sparq-core, under the existing 'parallel' feature, no new dep. Done-def: chunked Turtle uses the sharded merge on >=2 threads; single-thread path unchanged; ALL existing Turtle differential oracles stay green (parallel_turtle_*_match_serial, W3C TurtleTests positive+negative, the SPARQL fuzzer); bench/parse bench-ttl 8T-vs-1T scaling ratio improves over the serial-merge baseline on a quiet box (ratio is the durable claim, not absolute MB/s — canonical runner, NOT the EC2 work box). From sq-4wo research (research/parsing-perf-delta.md, lever T4).

title: ODRL bridge: deny revocation / retraction (remove a materialized auth:deny* when the prohibition no longer applies)
description: The sq-w693 bridge APPENDS an auth:deny<Mode> triple and is idempotent, but there is no path to RETRACT a materialized deny when the underlying ODRL prohibition is removed/expires or the carve-out no longer applies — the deny persists in the auth view until the next full re-materialization from static WAC/ACP (which does not know about bridged ODRL triples). Same gap exists for bridged Permit grants (sq-h3uk). Design a retraction/refresh path: either tag bridged triples with provenance so a targeted removal is possible, or define a re-evaluate-and-rebuild step for the ODRL-bridged subset. From sq-w693. Epic sq-3183.

title: ODRL bridge: constraint-conditional deny (materialize ACP-style conditional deny for constrained Prohibitions)
description: The sq-w693 prohibition bridge materializes an UNCONDITIONAL auth:deny<Mode> for a prohibition that matches the concrete request context. A prohibition whose carve-out is itself constrained (e.g. deny write ONLY when purpose=marketing) is only materialized for the specific request that satisfies the constraint — there is no standing conditional-deny node. Investigate emitting an auth:ConditionalGrant-style conditional DENY (the AuthIndex already supports conditional grants/denies via the cond path) so a constrained prohibition becomes a standing rule, not a per-request snapshot. From sq-w693. Epic sq-3183.

title: filtered-ANN: cost-model for when transitive masking is worth it
description: sq-3tjd always derives + evaluates the connected-component sub-BGP to build the IdMask whenever the neighbour variable is constrained. For a BROAD/non-selective transitive constraint, evaluating the whole connected sub-BGP up front (then filtered-scanning) may cost more than the plain unfiltered nearest_exact + post-filter. Build a cost-model / selectivity estimate that chooses between (a) transitive-mask filtered search and (b) unfiltered + post-filter, per request. Relates to filter.rs FilterConfig::prefer_prefilter selectivity crossover. From sq-3tjd. Epic sq-3183.

title: filtered-ANN: cyclic-join handling in transitive mask derivation
description: The connected-component mask derivation (sq-3tjd) follows shared variables transitively via a fixpoint worklist, which terminates and is correct for cyclic join-graphs (a cycle just means a variable is reached twice; the component is still well-defined). But it does NOT special-case or optimise cyclic sub-BGPs (e.g. detecting that a cycle is unsatisfiable cheaply, or ordering the evaluated sub-BGP for cyclic joins). Investigate whether cyclic constraining sub-BGPs need any special treatment for correctness under all FILTER/path shapes, and whether evaluation-order matters for cost. From sq-3tjd. Epic sq-3183.

title: SBOM: upstream cargo-cyclonedx path-ref fix + member-purl canonicalization edge cases
description: cargo-cyclonedx 0.5.9 raw output still stamps the absolute build dir into workspace/path-dependency bom-refs (path+file:///abs/...#ver) and purls (?download_url=file://...). sq-toze.30 fixed only the PUBLICATION path (scripts/sbom-normalize.jq applied in gen-sbom-vex.sh + supply-chain.yml#sbom). Remaining: (1) upstream cargo-cyclonedx so raw output is host-clean (or bump to a version that emits registry-style purls for path deps); (2) audit member-purl canonicalization edge cases the current jq pass simplifies (e.g. download_url query stripping vs proper pkg:cargo qualifiers, build-target sub-component purl fragments like #src/main.rs). From sq-toze.30. Epic sq-toze.

title: MPC: fresh coZK soundness re-audit (eprint 2025/1026) of the collaborative-proof path
description: From sq-pwr research (research/mpc-zkp-build-out-delta.md M-D). No crate directly — a research/audit deliverable governing sparq-mpc::proof + sparq-zk-compose when M4 v1 (sq-f7bu) / the M4 spike (sq-bjl) is built. Before ANY collaborative-proving soundness claim, adversarially validate against CRYPTO'25 coZK pitfalls (Garg-Goel-Jain-Roberts-Sekar eprint 2025/1026): proving on an inconsistent/extended witness can LEAK honest provers' inputs, and SOTA malicious compilers as-is are insecure in general; honest-majority semi-honest-prover ~= malicious-secure ONLY IF the extended witness is validated BEFORE proving; TACEO co-snarks (coNoir<->Barretenberg, the closest usable stack) is explicitly UNAUDITED and predates 2025/1026. Done: a written re-audit verdict (CLOSED/RE-OPEN per the 2025/1026 lenses) + a witness-validation requirement encoded as a test obligation on the collaborative path. DISTINCT from the external single-prover audit sq-qhy4 and from the UC/composition DESIGN records sq-aaop/sq-wj4k (this is an adversarial re-audit, not a design doc). Gates M-C/M-E production claims. Opt-in N/A (analysis).

title: MPC M4-v1: verifier-side authenticated-input attestation GATE assembly (Dutta/Artemis) -> verifiable federated response
description: From sq-pwr research (research/mpc-zkp-build-out-delta.md M-C). Crate: sparq-mpc (pipeline.rs/proof.rs) + sparq-zk-compose (federated reconstruct_public_inputs + bind_issuer_attestations reuse). The buildable M4 v1: each holder contributes secret-shared committed data, federated correctness/threshold runs in MPC, attestation (each C(G_i) signed by a key in K) checked VERIFIER-SIDE (Dutta authenticated-input eprint 2022/1648 + Artemis commit-and-prove anchor arXiv 2409.12055), byte-bound by a federated multi-source layout, with explicit freshness/replay binding (sig checked out-of-circuit so audit-#4 is not automatic). Consumes sq-34ml prerequisites; distinct from the DEFERRED in-circuit spike sq-bjl. Done: federated correctness + verifier-side attestation for the four-flatmates threshold with negative e2e tests (forged source / replayed manifest / out-of-K key REJECT). Opt-in (stays a single-prover UltraHonk verifier, canonical vk verifier-side). v1 GIVES UP source-unlinkability + a single succinct sig<->witness proof + malicious-against-N-1. BLOCKED for any production attestation claim until the coZK re-audit AND external audit sq-qhy4 land. Depends sq-34ml.

title: Federation TPF follow-ups: brTPF bind-restricted fragments + full Hydra paging vocab (first/last)
description: Follow-up to sq-bzh1/#282. brTPF (bind-restricted Triple Pattern Fragments for efficient federated joins) + hydra:first/hydra:last paging controls. Opt-in under the tpf feature. Epic sq-3183.

title: Revocation/refresh of bridged ODRL grants on policy change in AUTH_GRAPH bridge
description: The sq-h3uk bridge APPENDS a materialized ODRL grant to the auth view and reindexes, but never removes a previously-bridged grant when the underlying ODRL policy changes (e.g. a permission is withdrawn, a time window lapses, or a re-evaluation now Denies). Static WAC/ACP re-materialization rebuilds <urn:sparq:auth> wholesale, which would also drop bridged grants — so the two must be reconciled. Design a refresh model: track bridged grants distinctly (provenance), re-evaluate on policy change, and retract stale grants without clobbering static WAC/ACP grants. Stay fail-closed (a lapsed grant must lose access). Deferred from sq-h3uk. Epic sq-3183.

title: Richer ODRL constraint -> WAC/ACP conditional-grant mapping in AUTH_GRAPH bridge
description: The sq-h3uk bridge evaluates ODRL constraints (purpose/recipient/time/count) in sparq-policy and materializes a grant ONLY when they are satisfied for the supplied request context — the constraint is checked at materialization time, not carried into the auth view. Investigate mapping selected ODRL constraints onto sparq-solid's existing ACP conditional-grant / exceptMatcher machinery (auth:ConditionalGrant, acceptsAgentP/acceptsClientP) so a constraint can persist as a condition re-checked per session rather than baked into a one-shot grant. Stay fail-closed; only map constraints with a faithful WAC/ACP condition analogue. Deferred from sq-h3uk. Epic sq-3183.

title: ODRL Prohibition -> explicit auth:deny materialization in AUTH_GRAPH bridge
description: The sq-h3uk single-node bridge materializes only Permit -> auth:<mode> allow grants. Extend it to materialize a matched ODRL Prohibition as an explicit auth:denyRead/denyWrite/denyAppend/denyControl triple (deny-overrides) for the request's principal+target, so an ODRL carve-out becomes a concrete WAC/ACP deny honoured by the existing enforcement. Keep fail-closed and behind the odrl-bridge feature. Deferred from sq-h3uk. Epic sq-3183.
close_reason: Closed

title: Filtered-ANN vec:: cost-model choice of filtered-vs-post-filter
description: sq-bvmd ALWAYS uses the filtered search (nearest_exact_filtered over the derived mask) whenever a constraining pattern exists. For a BROAD mask (nearly the whole store satisfies the BGP) plain unfiltered nearest_exact + post-filter the top-k can be cheaper, and DiskAnnIndex::nearest_filtered already switches strategy by selectivity (FilterConfig). Add a cost-model that, given mask selectivity / store size, chooses filtered-search vs post-filtering vs which filtered strategy. Deferred from sq-bvmd. Epic sq-3183.

title: Filtered-ANN vec:: mask caching across prepares
description: sq-bvmd re-evaluates the constraining sub-BGP (a SELECT through the engine) on every prepare_vec to build the IdMask. For repeated queries against an unchanged graph+store this re-derives the same mask. Cache the derived IdMask keyed by (sub-BGP, graph fingerprint), invalidated on graph/store change. Deferred from sq-bvmd. Epic sq-3183.

title: Filtered-ANN vec:: multi-variable mask intersection
description: The sq-bvmd BGP->IdMask wiring derives the candidate mask from patterns that constrain the SINGLE vec: neighbour variable. When several vec: requests share constraining patterns, or a neighbour is constrained transitively through a second variable (e.g. ?node :owns ?x . ?x a :Vehicle), the mask could be the INTERSECTION across the joined sub-BGP rather than just direct mentions of ?node. Implement multi-variable / transitive mask derivation (evaluate the join-connected sub-BGP, project the neighbour var). Deferred from sq-bvmd. Epic sq-3183.
close_reason: Closed

title: ZK car-hire: wire remaining circuit-family members (scan/join/hidden_issuer/revoke/holder_pok) into in-browser bb.js proving
description: The /showcase/zk-car-hire flagship proves the age-gate sub-proof (filter_int_d2) LIVE in the browser via @noir-lang/noir_js + @aztec/bb.js UltraHonk, against a committed ACIR artifact (site/public/zk/filter_int_d2.json). Remaining flagship sub-proofs are real sparq circuits (compiled + gate-counted) but are presented as 'composed' (not yet in-tab): scan_k2_n64_r8 (BGP per credential graph), join_eq_na16_nb16 (same-holder without disclosure), hidden_issuer_d4 (trusted-issuer set membership), revoke_unset_d10 (non-revocation at hidden index), holder_pok (holder-key possession). Wire these into the browser to prove the FULL car-hire ProofManifest in-tab, and add a verifier-side bind_joins(k=2) check. Each circuit needs: nargo compile -> ship ACIR to public/zk/; a witness builder (the native sparq-zk-compose toml/build helpers compute operand_enc/commitments/Merkle roots, which must be reproduced or precomputed as fixtures for the browser); and manifest composition. Note the documented gap: DOB->age is not an in-circuit derivation (the credential must carry an integer age claim). Honesty framing (research-grade, NOT externally audited, sq-qhy4/CR-G1) must remain. Refs: sq-13rg, sq-4r4b.

title: [cert][gap ASVS-G3] Verify sparq-server engine error strings never leak filesystem paths/internal hosts — ASVS V7.1.1
description: ASVS V7.1.1: error responses must not disclose internal detail. sparq-server json_error (crates/sparq-server/src/http.rs:2671) returns a structured {error:msg}; engine parse/exec messages are ECHOED to the client by design (query-author UX). These are not deliberately path/host-bearing, but there is no test ASSERTING that a parse/exec error never contains an absolute path, a SERVICE host, or an internal addr. Remediation: audit engine_error_response/execution_error message sources; add a regression test that error bodies for a crafted query/file do not contain '/' filesystem prefixes or resolved host:port. Ref sq-toze / sq-toze.10. [OPUS-4.8]

title: [cert][gap ASVS-G1] sparq-server emits no security headers (X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff at minimum) — ASVS V14.4
description: ASVS V14.4 expects baseline security response headers. sparq-server (crates/sparq-server/src/http.rs) sets no X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options, CSP, or HSTS. Residual risk LOW (JSON API, no HTML sink, no cookies) but nosniff is cheap and expected. Remediation: add a tower layer setting 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' (and, for the JSON API, 'Cache-Control: no-store' on error/auth responses) on all responses; add a regression test asserting the header. Ref epic sq-toze / sq-toze.10 (ASVS). [OPUS-4.8]

title: [cert][cryptoreview] FIPS posture statement for sparq crypto (CMVP-absent, honest negative claim) + operator FIPS-deployment guidance
description: CR-G4 (LOW/AUDIT-READY). sparq uses NO FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic module and makes no FIPS claim. The bespoke ZK primitives (BN254, Poseidon2, Schnorr-over-Baby-JubJub) are NOT FIPS-approved algorithms (chosen for in-circuit efficiency). SHA-256 release digests are FIPS 180-4 but used for integrity outside any CMVP module. Document this honestly so an operator with a FIPS deployment constraint knows the Tier-B crypto is out of FIPS scope (and is publish=false / not in the default dependency graph anyway). Add a short FIPS note to SECURITY.md or the crypto crate READMEs. Ref sq-toze.

title: [cert][cryptoreview] Constant-time / side-channel analysis of the secret-bearing crypto paths (issuer signing, MPC shares) — dudect/ctgrind measurement
description: CR-G5 (P2). sparq has done NO formal constant-time analysis and NO dudect/ctgrind timing measurement. Today the Schnorr VERIFY path is verifier-side over public commitments (no long-term secret in the timing-sensitive path), and the MPC mask draw is documented effectively-CT-in-expectation (rng.rs:45) — so the present exposure is low. BUT: the issuer SIGNING path (secret key) is un-analysed, arkworks BN254 field ops are not asserted constant-time, and if the in-circuit hidden-key / in-circuit signature upgrades land (epic sq-1s2) the secret-bearing surface grows and CT becomes load-bearing. Run a dudect/ctgrind pass on sig.rs signing + the MPC share ops; document accepted leakage. Ref sq-toze + sq-1s2.

Add a CRA-style support-period statement to SECURITY.md (or a SUPPORT.md), e.g. 'security support provided for the latest published release; minimum support period <N> months from a release; EOL policy <...>'. Audit-ready: needs maintainer org decision on the actual period. Framework: cra. Evidence: compliance/cra/controls.md row II-A.6. [OPUS-4.8]

[cert][gap GX-12] No container-image vulnerability scan (Trivy/Grype) + Dockerfile-lint (Dockle/Hadolint) lane in CI
description: CIS framework (engineer: cert-cis). The Dockerfile ships a hardened distroless/nonroot/SHA-pinned image (verified) and a docker-smoke run gate exists (ci.yml docker-smoke + release.yml docker job), but there is NO automated container-image CVE scan (Trivy/Grype) nor a CIS-Docker-Benchmark Dockerfile linter (Dockle/Hadolint) lane in CI — confirmed by grep over .github/workflows (only false-positive comment matches in zk-toolchain.yml/ci-summary.yml). buildkit attaches an SBOM + SLSA provenance to the pushed image (release.yml docker: provenance=mode=max, sbom:true) but does not SCAN it for vulns. GAP maps to CIS Controls v8 7.5/7.6 (continuous/automated vuln scanning), 16.x (application security), 4.x (secure config of the container artifact) and CIS Docker Benchmark §4 (image build hardening). title: Fully-oblivious batched hidden join: secret-shared match bit (no per-pair open)
description: Follow-up to sq-khf9. HiddenValueJoin::batched_join currently decides each candidate's match with secure_equal, which OPENS the match bit per pair (decision-time L2 leak / match-graph + key fan-out). The oblivious OUTPUT transform (sq-jnkm) already hides the result cardinality/ordering, but to close L2 at its source the batched join must feed oblivious_set_output with MatchBit::SecretShared bits derived from the secret keys WITHOUT opening them — a secure equality-to-shared-bit (Rabbit/edaBits bit-decomposition over F_p). That consumes a multiplication chain and so depends on the BGW/DN degree-reduction round (sq-dvuc) and the secure-comparison primitive (sq-rrz4). Once those land, wire batched_join's candidate loop to produce SecretShared match bits and route through oblivious_set_output_hidden_keys instead of opening via secure_equal. Until then batched_join is honestly semi-honest with a documented decision-time match-bit open.

title: MPC/core: AddressSanitizer CI lane for the mmap unsafe sites Miri can't reach (B5)
description:
Follow-up to sq-fo28 (Miri lane). Miri STRUCTURALLY CANNOT run sparq-core's mmap-backed
unsafe surface — it rejects file-backed memory mappings ("Miri does not support file-backed
memory mappings"), so the 16 mmap sites (every memmap2::Mmap::map / MmapMut::map_mut /
madvise, the libc sysconf/statvfs FFI in dict-spill, and every slice reinterpret whose
provenance is a live Mmap) are uncovered by the Miri lane.

AddressSanitizer CAN instrument real mmap, so it is the right tool to add UB/OOB coverage
over the B5 on-disk-index loader (the mmap_corruption_oracle + dict-spill paths) under real
file-backed mappings.

DEFERRED from the sq-fo28 PR (the bead asked to add ASan only if clean+cheap, else bead it):
ASan needs -Zsanitizer=address + RUSTFLAGS + likely -Zbuild-std on a sanitizer-compatible
(non-musl) target, and combining it with mmap + rayon can be flaky — not worth blocking the
Miri PR on. The existing deterministic mmap_corruption_oracle (ci.yml --features mmap,dict-spill)
+ the fuzz lane's mmap-loader target already exercise B5 for panics/OOM; ASan would add the
UB/OOB-under-real-mmap signal.

Scope: add a nightly-only `.github/workflows/` job (or extend miri.yml) running
`cargo +nightly -Zbuild-std -Zsanitizer=address test -p sparq-core --features mmap,dict-spill`
against x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, SHA-pinned actions, NOT a per-PR gate. Validate it is clean
+ non-flaky before making it a standing lane.

title: MPC: in-protocol range proof of the secret-shared sum bound (make disclose_threshold_verdict's sum-magnitude precondition fail-closed)
description: Follow-up from sq-g7t5/PR #168. disclose_threshold_verdict range-checks public_threshold fail-closed, but the SECRET sum's magnitude bound is currently a CALLER PRECONDITION that cannot be validated from shares — violation is silently wrong with no in-protocol guard. Add an in-protocol range proof / bit-length bound on the shared sum so an out-of-range sum is rejected rather than producing a wrong verdict. Security-hardening; closes the documented seam. [OPUS-4.8]

title: MPC: deployment-grade in-MPC bit-decomposition for disclose_threshold_verdict (random-bit sub-protocol + wider magnitude + malicious-secure)
description: Follow-up to sq-g7t5. sq-g7t5 landed a CORRECT honest-majority, semi-honest in-MPC bit-decomposition of the secret-shared sum (masked-open / Damgaard et al. TCC'06) inside disclose_threshold_verdict (crates/sparq-mpc/src/compare.rs): the local reconstruct(sum_shares) shortcut is GONE; the sum is masked with fresh dealer randomness [r], only c = sum + r is opened (statistically hiding, gap kappa=40 bits), the sum's bits are recovered by a secret-shared bitwise-subtraction borrow chain, and ONLY the verdict bit is opened. Residual deployment work (NOT done in sq-g7t5): (1) RANDOM-BIT SUB-PROTOCOL — solved-bits are dealt by the in-process dealer (deal_random_solved_bits), legitimate in the single-process sim but in a real deployment no party may know r; replace with a real random-bit protocol (square-protocol: p=2^61-1 is 3 mod 4 so public sqrt exists; or edaBits Crypto'20). (2) MAGNITUDE BOUND — p=2^61-1 forces DECOMP_VALUE_BITS=20 (covers 4-flatmates 10^6, not larger); lift via a larger field or a non-masked-open comparison (Rabbit eprint 2021/119). (3) MALICIOUS SECURITY — every mul/degree_reduce in the chain is semi-honest-only; carry IT-MACs (sq-km34.x) through and MAC-check the boolean verdict before open (design-doc Hole 4, research/mpc-malicious-security-design.md). [OPUS-4.8]

title: sparq-shacl: expose a callable SHACL-validation API for external/JS consumers (PSS) — decide binding (WASM vs N-API vs HTTP service)

Needs PSS/user input on deployment shape (in-process vs sidecar). Parity finding also corroborates the sq-55c1 differential-fuzz suite. [OPUS-4.8]

title: bench: geo/GeoSPARQL suite — result-count + compliance-pass gate + geosparql-jena compliance peer + PostGIS loose ref
description:
Design: capability-benchmark-program.md §3.5. Workload: Geographica dataset + galbiston geosparql-benchmarking Micro Benchmark (1-2 triple-pattern spatial-function queries) + bench_geo example (100k CRS84 points) + GeoSPARQL Compliance Benchmark (Jovanovik) coverage score.
DETERMINISTIC gate (mode:auto): result-set size of each geof:/within/nearest query over a fixed point corpus + a geo_compliance_pass ratchet (functions/reqs passing, only tightens; emit as deficit max_funcs-passed, G4). Floating-point geometry -> gate COUNTS and PASS/FAIL, never coordinate values. TIMING advisory: geo_within10km_us, _nearest_k10_us, _index_build_s.
Competitors: Compliance bar = GeoSPARQL-Jena / Fuseki-geosparql (Apache-2.0, docker; only triplestore with full GML+WKT — right like-for-like since sparq-geo does both; adapter http-sparql). Perf peers Virtuoso/GraphDB are WKT-only (asymmetry; GraphDB not fully open). Loose lower bound = PostGIS (relational, no geof:/graph joins; the rstar sub-component, NOT a SPARQL competitor; match CRS/op semantics — planar/equirectangular vs geodesic — or unfair).
notes: SPARQ agent. Per-surface benchmark suite from research/capability-benchmark-program.md (PR #160). Follows the recipe in §1; SHACL lead = sq-7iai; shared competitor adapter infra = sq-eifd.
close_reason: Landed on main via PR #184 (merged): GeoSPARQL bench suite (bench/geo/) — within/nearest/geof: count gate + geo_compliance_deficit ratchet (now HARD-gated — fixed floor:0 silently skipping), geosparql-jena/PostGIS competitors. Dashboard-conflict resolved (all 3 suite rows kept), Copilot review resolved. 115 tests. [OPUS-4.8]

title: bench: full-text suite — hit-count + bytes/doc gate (+BEIR recall/nDCG) + jena-text surface peer + Lucene kernel ref
description:
Design: capability-benchmark-program.md §3.4. Two axes: IR-quality (small redistributable BEIR/MS-MARCO cut — TREC-COVID or SciFact + qrels, loaded as RDF literals -> Recall@100/nDCG@10) and latency (existing bench_text example: 1M synthetic 8-word literals, ~10k Zipf vocab; AND/OR/prefix/phrase).
DETERMINISTIC gate (mode:auto): result/hit count for a fixed query set (text:matches/phrase/near) + index bytes-per-doc (integer-exact). With BEIR wired, Recall@100/nDCG@10 as deficits (G4). TIMING advisory: text_and_us/_prefix_us/_build_s.
Competitors: BE HONEST — Solr/ES are NOT SPARQL competitors (off the dashboard). (1) Surface peer = Apache Jena Fuseki + jena-text Lucene SAIL (Apache-2.0, docker) — only like-for-like FTS-over-SPARQL. (2) Kernel ref = Lucene (EMBEDDED lib, not Solr server — sparq-text is embedded) via Anserini for BM25 on BEIR (Apache-2.0); its OWN IR harness/bead, labelled "sub-component, not an RDF benchmark". Scope kernel comparison to what sparq implements (AND/OR, prefix, phrase, slop, BM25 k1=1.2/b=0.75).
notes: SPARQ agent. Per-surface benchmark suite from research/capability-benchmark-program.md (PR #160). Follows the recipe in §1; SHACL lead = sq-7iai; shared competitor adapter infra = sq-eifd.

Copilot review resolved: no-arg run reproduces pinned corpus (seed 0, N=100k), FTS hook skips PR tier, README metric names fixed. 58 tests. [OPUS-4.8]

title: bench: vector/ANN suite — promote tests/recall floors to recall-deficit gate + ann-benchmarks recall-QPS + hnswlib/FAISS/ScaNN/DiskANN

title: bench: reasoning suite extensions — DeepTax per-commit self-gate + closure_triples metric + reasonable/Nemo/VLog competitors
description:
Extend the already-~80%-wired reasoning estate (LUBM has the full treatment; bench/inference/ has deeptax gen + EYE). Design: capability-benchmark-program.md §3.2. Highest-value cheap wins first:
- A4: promote DeepTaxonomy to a self-gating bench/inference/deeptax/run.sh (hard-assert closure size dt1k/10k/100k = N+1; closes gap G5 — DT is featured but not yet a per-commit hook).
- A5: add <suite>_closure_triples (mode:auto) across ALL reasoning suites — the single most valuable reasoner gate (catches silent under-derivation where no query touches).
- A1: LUBM scaled tiers lubm-8/lubm-100 (EC2/nightly; per-commit stays LUBM(1); gen.sh already -univ-parameterized; generate expected-rows-univ8/100.tsv once).
- A3: owl:sameAs equality micro-suite (in-script clique of N x M; closure size is a closed form -> hard gate, no download).
- A2/A6 (later): UOBM (RL-approx TBox; gather-only generator) + OWL2Bench RL profile (CC-BY-4.0).
Competitors (beyond EYE): reasonable (gtfierro, BSD-3, Rust OWL-RL materializer — ADD FIRST, embeddable like Oxigraph -> differential closure-size oracle); Jena rules (Apache-2.0, JVM correctness oracle, no rule authoring); Nemo + VLog (Apache-2.0, docker, supply RL/RDFS rules once — completes the RR-2023 set); RDFox (proprietary, license-gated -> needs:user). DO NOT benchmark OWL-DL classifiers (Pellet/HermiT/ELK) for materialization. Cross-check closure_triples before timing.

description:

First-party, actively maintained openlink/virtuoso-opensource-7 image; isql ld_dir + rdf_loader_run bulk-loads NT/TTL; serves SPARQL 1.1 -> runs all existing sparq suites.

title: zk-toolchain: gate forge-suite by changed-files on merge_group to skip ~60min run on non-zk queue entries
description: The merge_group event does not honour on.pull_request.paths filters, so zk-toolchain.yml's bare merge_group: trigger runs the full ~60min nargo/bb forge suite on EVERY merge-queue enqueue, not only zk-touching ones (unlike PRs, which are paths-gated). Hang-free + correct (ci-summary discovers the present check-set per-ref), but wasteful. Optimisation: add a job-level changed-files gate to forge-suite keyed on github.event.merge_group.base_sha (diff base_sha..HEAD against crates/sparq-zk/**, crates/sparq-zk-compose/**, zk/**, .github/workflows/zk-toolchain.yml); short-circuit to a green no-op when no zk paths changed, matching PR behaviour. Avoid new third-party actions (SHA-pin discipline) — a plain git-diff step is enough. Introduced with the merge-queue trigger PR (ci-merge-group-triggers). [OPUS-4.8]

title: MPC: bounded property-path — {1,k}/{0,k}/p? + alternation as union-of-fixed-chains with OR-fold length-dedup (each endpoint pair once, realized length never revealed)
description:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent (jeswr/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine). Filed by the SPARQ agent (not PSS). [OPUS-4.8]

Increment #3 of sq-py8h (design §2.2–2.5, §6). Build the bounded repetition and alternation on top of the exactly-k chain (#2): {1,k} = union of length-1..k chains; {0,k} = {1,k} plus the reflexive length-0 diagonal (?a=?b, chain bit = constant shared 1); p? = {0,1}; alternation (p1|p2){h} = union of (branches)^h fixed chains. The secret-shared connected-bit = OR-fold (1 - prod(1 - c_l)) over the union, built from mul_shares_raw + degree_reduce (AND/NOT) — this collapses multiplicity ACROSS chain lengths so each endpoint pair appears once WITHOUT revealing which length connected it (length-revealing prohibition, design §1.2). Reuses oblivious_set_output for the padded+shuffled reveal.
acceptance_criteria: Differential test passes: {1,k}, {0,k}, p?, alternation all == clear-text bounded-path evaluation; each connected endpoint pair returned exactly once; realized length never opened; reflexive diagonal correct for {0,k}/p?.

title: MPC: bounded property-path — hidden-intermediate fixed exactly-k chain (secret-shared k-hop join chaining match bits via degree_reduce; intermediate nodes never opened)
description:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent (jeswr/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine). Filed by the SPARQ agent (not PSS). [OPUS-4.8]

Increment #2 (core cryptographic deliverable) of sq-py8h (design §2.1, §6). The secret-shared k-hop chain: each hop is a HiddenValueJoin/secure_equal-class equi-join (join.rs:411) whose match bit is kept SECRET-SHARED (never opened — closes L2 at source); conjunction of the k hop bits via mul_shares_raw (shamir.rs:670) + degree_reduce (shamir.rs:406, the sq-dvuc keystone, now merged) so the chain bit chains across all k hops at degree t. Intermediate nodes ?z_i never reconstructed. Final connected-bit fed into oblivious_set_output (oblivious_join.rs:254) with a public padded bound B; reveal B shuffled slots. Semi-honest honest-majority; inherits (does not worsen) the degree-2t-at-n=2t+1 residual (sq-6d6g/sq-km34).
acceptance_criteria: Differential test passes: secure hidden-intermediate exactly-k chain == plaintext bounded-path join over the union, keys NEVER reconstructed; intermediate node-sets stay secret-shared; per-pair match bit never opened; output is padded+shuffled to B.

title: MPC: bounded property-path — disclosed-key regime (unroll fixed-k path over disclosed global IRIs to a DisclosedKeyJoin fold + union + dedup, crypto-free)
description:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent (jeswr/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine). Filed by the SPARQ agent (not PSS). [OPUS-4.8]

Increment #1 of the sq-py8h bounded property-path operator (design: research/mpc-bounded-property-path-design.md §6). Unroll a bounded path a (p){m,k} b over DISCLOSED global-IRI keys to a fixed sequence of DisclosedKeyJoin folds (one fixed BGP chain per length m..k), unioned and deduplicated, recomputed OUTSIDE the crypto core (convention #4). No new crypto — reuses DisclosedKeyJoin (join.rs:119) exactly as differential_three_holder_chain_equals_union (a 3-pattern unroll). Closes the headline federation case where endpoints are disclosed global IRIs. Differential test: federated unroll == clear-text eval_path over the union store for the bounded form.
acceptance_criteria: Differential test passes: bounded-path unroll over disclosed keys == clear-text bounded-path evaluation over the union store; supports seq, exact {k}, {m,k}, {0,k} reflexive, alternation; dedups endpoint pairs; no MPC rounds.
close_reason: Landed on main via PR #174 (merged): MPC bounded property-path disclosed-key regime — unroll to DisclosedKeyJoin folds + union + dedup over disclosed global IRIs (seq/{k}/{m,k}/{0,k}/p?/alternation), crypto-free (no MPC rounds). Copilot review resolved with real fixes: unroll DoS guard (MAX_UNROLL_CHAINS + checked count), vacuous crypto-free test fixed via negative control, {m,n} history doc corrected. 235 tests. [OPUS-4.8]

title: sparq-solid: support acp:CreatorAgent / acp:OwnerAgent via trusted loader-synthesized solidx:creator/owner facts

title: sparq-solid: DECISION — ldp:contains/containment view ownership (PSS-written explicit triples vs sparq-derived); structural-derivation spike only if PSS wants it
description: [OPUS-4.8] sq-3jtd re-materialization scope (OUT-OF-SCOPE-FOR-NOW, decision-tracking). Today ldp:contains is fixture data only (fixture.rs:75-84) — stored/queryable, never derived or re-materialized on a write; containment ancestry is derived structurally (solidx:parent/ancestor) ONLY for ACL inheritance. PSS writes ldp:contains explicitly in its UPDATE bodies (gh-48). RECOMMENDED: keep it PSS-written (avoids re-derive-on-every-write, keeps the §2.4 content/reasoner security boundary clean, and the atomic multi-op UPDATE sq-ycle keeps it consistent). This bead tracks the decision; only spike a structural-only sparq-side derivation IF PSS later asks sparq to own it. research/sparq-solid-scope.md area 2.

title: sparq-solid: RESEARCH record — incremental auth-view maintenance under stratified NAF (counting/DRed/partial-cache-invalidation vs ~1s full rebuild)
description: [OPUS-4.8] sq-3jtd re-materialization scope (RESEARCH-OPEN). Full N3 rebuild on every ACL change invalidates all session caches (~1.0s WAC / ~1.1s ACP on the 1.1k-graph fixture). The honest blocker: sparq-reason exact-derivation-counting (MaterializedGraph 'T18') is RDFS-only and does NOT know NAF, but the ACP rules use stratified negation-as-failure (log:notIncludes). Survey counting/DRed/differential-dataflow under stratified NAF + partial session-cache invalidation via the solidx:ancestor dependency map (only drop entries whose authorized set could change). Determine whether any beats the measured ~1s full rebuild at realistic pod scale BEFORE implementing. Conceptually depends on sq-jwsp (reason_n3_stratified). research/sparq-solid-scope.md area 2 + research/solid-access-control-design.md §4.2/§7.3.

title: MPC: adversarial tests — a tampering party is CAUGHT (the witness the upgrade is real)
description: sq-km34 design sec 6.8. Extend crates/sparq-mpc/src/adversarial_tests.rs: a malicious party that (a) forges a product share at n=2t+1, (b) feeds a wrong re-sharing in degree_reduce (shamir.rs:457), (c) shares an inconsistent (non-degree-t) input, (d) biases the equality mask r toward a chosen value - EACH must abort with MpcError::MacCheckFailed, and the honest path must still pass. title: MPC: secure threshold/comparison primitive (secret-shared greater-than for the £100k aggregate verdict, opens only the boolean)
description: The driving use case (architecture §4.3 step 4, four-flatmates) is proving cumulative-salary > £100k while disclosing ONLY the boolean verdict, not the exact sum. Today run_secure computes the linear sum and reconstruct_disclosed opens the integer, so the verifier recomputes the threshold on a DISCLOSED aggregate — leaking the exact total (violating disclosure-minimisation in §4.3 step 3). A secret-shared comparison (bit-decomposition or constant-round less-than over Fp) opening only the match bit is the missing primitive; it reuses the equality-style masked-open in join.rs plus bit-extraction. Secure greater-than is multiplication-depth>1, hence the degree-reduction dependency. Differential test: secure verdict == plaintext (sum > threshold); the exact sum is never opened.

title: MPC: BGW/DN degree-reduction round so secret-shared multiplications can chain

Any computation deeper than one multiplication (secure comparison/threshold, products of match conditions, conjunctive hidden-pattern joins) is impossible because the degree is never reduced to t. Standard fix: one re-share-and-recombine round (BGW with a public reduction matrix, or DN double-sharings) over the existing in-process party simulation. Acceptance: degree-reduce(shares_2t)->shares_t that round-trips + a two-multiplication chain test (a*b*c) matching plaintext. The hard dependency for the actual £100k threshold verdict.

title: Audit every untrusted-on-disk-file loader for unbounded pre-allocation (OOM-DoS), workspace-wide
description: sq-f5jh capped two unbounded untrusted-`n` pre-allocations in sparq-core's on-disk loaders: TripleStore::load_pred_stats (predstats.bin record count -> FxHashMap::reserve(n)) and the legacy Dict::open (dict.bin np/nd/nt counts -> Vec::with_capacity + read_str's vec![0u8; n] string lengths), both now clamped to the actual file length. The mmap dict + compressed-perm loaders were already capped (sq-znld/sq-ed2i). DEEPER: this OOM-on-hostile-length pattern (read a count/length from an attacker-controlled file, feed it straight to with_capacity/reserve/vec![0;n] BEFORE checking it against the remaining bytes) likely recurs in OTHER crates' on-disk index loaders that were never audited: sparq-vectors (HNSW/DiskANN on-disk indexes), sparq-hdt (HDT archive sections), sparq-text/sparq-geo (any persisted index), sparq-zk (proof/key blobs). Each is a potential uncatchable OOM-abort DoS on a corrupt/hostile file. WORK: grep each crate's src for with_capacity/reserve/vec![0; n]/read_exact-after-length on bytes that originate from a file read; cap every such allocation against the file/slice length (claimed n * min_element_size <= remaining_bytes) before allocating, fail-closed with the existing error. Add a corruption-oracle-style sweep where a loader is security-relevant. Pattern + rationale: see crates/sparq-core/src/dict.rs (read_str_bounded/read_str_bounded_io) and store.rs load_pred_stats. [OPUS-4.8]
close_reason: Closed

title: Bound writer-queue head-of-line blocking from a slow SPARQL UPDATE
description: Discovered while wiring sq-ebii UPDATE timeout. The query timeout now applies to UPDATE: the WHERE eval runs under a cooperative QueryBudget on the writer thread (deadline + memory cap), and the HTTP await is hard-capped (timeout + grace -> 503). RESIDUAL GAP: updates are SEQUENCED on a single writer (sparq-serve group-commit), so while a slow update runs its WHERE to its cooperative stop, every queued update behind it waits — the timeout bounds the offending client's wait, not the writer's work, and not the head-of-line blocking of the queue. Options: (a) pre-flight the WHERE pattern's cost / run it under budget BEFORE entering the sequenced apply so the writer never starts an over-budget WHERE; (b) shorter writer-side deadline for the WHERE phase; (c) reject obviously-expensive updates at parse time. Measure first. [OPUS-4.8]

title: Byte-accounted per-request memory cap for sparq-server (true RSS quota)
description: Follow-up to sq-ebii. The sq-ebii memory cap (--max-query-rows) is a COARSE working-set ROW ceiling, not a byte/RSS quota: it bounds materialised intermediate/final row COUNT via the engine QueryBudget.max_rows, so a query with few but very WIDE rows (many projected vars / huge string literals), or non-row allocations (dictionary growth on UPDATE, CONSTRUCT templates, sort/group scratch), can still exceed the implied memory. Implement a true byte-accounted allocator/arena cap (or instrument peak heap per request) so the server can enforce a real per-request memory ceiling and refuse (413) before crossing it. Likely needs an engine-level allocation-accounting seam (a budget on BYTES, not just rows) threaded like the existing QueryBudget thread-local. [OPUS-4.8]

description: Jesse: a Pages-hosted docs site with NO content duplication across locations — if content must appear in both a README and the docs, COPY it at docs-build time (not maintained twice). design:
Docs-website design (research agent sq-w9sr, 2026-06-14). READ-ONLY research; nothing in repo modified.

ARCHITECTURE: one Pages site, GitHub-Actions source. / = mdBook guide; /api = `cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps`; /dev/bench = EXISTING benchmark dashboard preserved (folded into the same artifact at deploy time).

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: Pages Source is a single global mutually-exclusive setting. Today bench.yml publishes to the orphan `benchmark-data` branch via legacy "deploy from a branch" mode (Settings->Pages -> benchmark-data/(root)). Switching to "GitHub Actions" stops the branch being published, so docs.yml MUST re-include the dashboard each run: checkout benchmark-data -> copy dev/bench into ./book artifact. bench.yml stays the PRODUCER; docs.yml becomes the PUBLISHER. The Source flip is a one-time owner action (needs:user).

ANTI-DRIFT (load-bearing): mdBook {{#include path:anchor}} / {{#rustdoc_include test.rs:anchor}} single-source from real files (anchors = `// ANCHOR:`/`<!-- ANCHOR: -->`). mdBook EXITS 0 on broken include/anchor (rust-lang/mdBook#1094) -> MUST grep build log for [ERROR] AND run `mdbook test`. Tested examples = fragments of real `tests/`/`examples/` files cargo-test already runs. README<->rustdoc direction = README-as-source via include_str! (sq-p26u); do NOT add cargo-rdme (opposite direction, fights sq-9jw5 human-first template). jscpd for duplication detection (threshold:0, minTokens~80, scoped to README/skills/docs/research/book, reporters incl threshold).

BOUNDARIES (no overlap): link-check/markdownlint/Vale/typos/length/no-perf -> sq-5fd1. include_str!/docs.rs-metadata/cargo-test--doc gate -> sq-p26u. concise READMEs+logo -> sq-9jw5. sq-w9sr owns ONLY: mdBook scaffold, Pages deploy + bench reconciliation, {{#include}} wiring, tested-example embedding, broken-include [ERROR] grep, jscpd job.

TOOLS: mdbook 0.4 + mdbook-linkcheck (or mdbook-keeper if inline blocks need workspace deps); actions/configure-pages@v5 + upload-pages-artifact@v3 + deploy-pages@v5 (SHA-pin all). Doc jobs feed $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (the repo "ci-summary" pattern).

title: Document/guard SERVICE-feature SSRF: no allowlist/denylist on federated endpoint fetch
description: The SPARQL SERVICE clause is OFF by default in the shipped server (engine 'service' feature not enabled; verified ureq absent from sparq-server dep tree). But if a deployer enables the 'service' feature, HttpTransport::fetch (crates/sparq-engine/src/service.rs:208) POSTs to the endpoint IRI verbatim with ZERO SSRF protection: no block on 127.0.0.1/localhost, RFC1918, or cloud-metadata 169.254.169.254, only a 30s timeout. Combined with the unauthenticated server this is an open SSRF primitive into the internal network. Fix: add an endpoint allowlist/denylist (default-deny private/loopback/link-local/metadata ranges) gated by config, and document the risk in skills/http-server/SKILL.md. Note: sq-ebii already tracks the broader server DoS/SSRF-policy doc; this bead is the engine-side guard. Identified in research/threat-model.md (T-SERVICE-SSRF).
notes: [OPUS-4.8] branch sec-server-posture: did the IN-SCOPE (server-crate) half = DOCUMENTATION. The actual egress filter must live in crates/sparq-engine/src/service.rs (HttpTransport::fetch), which was OUT of this branch's scope (server crate only). Documented the SERVICE SSRF sharp edge where a server deployer looks: crates/sparq-server/README.md 'Security posture' section + skills/http-server/SKILL.md (SERVICE is OFF in the shipped server — engine 'service' feature not enabled, ureq absent from server dep tree; if enabled it is an un-filtered SSRF primitive). REMAINING engine-side implementation spec for whoever picks this up: in HttpTransport::fetch, before POSTing, resolve the endpoint host and DEFAULT-DENY if it resolves to a loopback (127.0.0.0/8, ::1), RFC1918 (10/8,172.16/12,192.168/16), link-local (169.254/16 incl. the 169.254.169.254 cloud-metadata IP, fe80::/10), unique-local (fc00::/7), unspecified (0.0.0.0/::) or other non-global range; gate an opt-in allowlist via engine config (mirror update.rs's with_load_base allowlist pattern). Must filter the RESOLVED IP (resolve-then-check) to defeat DNS rebinding, not just the literal IRI host. Tests: a unit IP-range classifier (each blocked range + a public IP passes) + a transport test asserting a loopback/metadata endpoint is refused with the feature on. Keep behind the existing 'service' feature. NOT pushed/merged.
close_reason: Landed: engine SERVICE SSRF default-deny egress filter (ureq Resolver, DNS-rebinding-safe) + opt-in allowlist, 16 tests. Server config -> sq-4w18. Gated+merged.

title: Validate compressed-perm header arithmetic (n_blocks/blocks_len overflow + unchecked block offsets/varints) in mmap loader
description: CompressedPerm::from_mmap (crates/sparq-core/src/compress.rs:147) checks FILE_MAGIC and a header-length equality, but (a) computes n_blocks*16 and dir_end+blocks_len in usize with NO overflow guard (a hostile n_blocks/blocks_len near u64::MAX can wrap so the equality passes against an undersized file), and (b) never validates the per-block byte offsets in the directory against blocks_len before feeding them to decode_block_at (compress.rs:188) whose get_varint (compress.rs:38) reads buf[*pos] with no bounds check and uses an attacker-controlled varint as a loop bound -> panic/OOB-read on a corrupt compressed .spq perm file. Fix: checked_mul/checked_add the header arithmetic, bounds-check every directory offset and varint read. Part of the same hostile-file fuzzing surface as sq-ky2a. Identified in research/threat-model.md (T-MMAP-DoS).
close_reason: Landed: CompressedPerm::from_mmap checked header arithmetic + bounded varints + decode-validate at open. Gated+merged.

title: Bound SPARQL parser recursion depth (stack-overflow DoS on deeply-nested query)
description: Vendored peg-based spargebra (vendor/spargebra/src/parser.rs) has NO recursion-depth, nesting-depth, or input-size limit. Recursive grammar rules (SubSelect, nested GroupGraphPattern, Expression->BrackettedExpression->Expression) map nesting depth onto native call-stack depth, so a query with thousands of nested '(' or '{' overflows the stack and aborts the process. Reachable from production PreparedQuery::parse (crates/sparq-engine/src/lib.rs:380) and the unauthenticated HTTP /sparql endpoint. The only existing guard is a TEST-HARNESS 20s watchdog (crates/sparq-conformance/src/run.rs:194) which does not protect production callers. Fix: add a depth/size cap (or stacker-style stack-growth guard) in the parse entry, contribute upstream per the vendoring policy. Identified in research/threat-model.md (T-PARSE-DoS).
close_reason: Landed: recursion-depth cap (128) in vendored spargebra; clean TooDeeplyNested error instead of stack-overflow abort. 12 tests; conformance 1229 (0 legit queries rejected); clippy clean. Upstream PR text recorded for oxigraph/spargebra. Merged.

title: External disk-spilling N-Triples builder lacks RDF 1.2 triple-term support
description: Follow-up to sq-hxgb. The in-MEMORY N-Triples loader now accepts <<( s p o )>> triple-term objects (nt::parse_chunk) and routes any triple-term-containing document to the serial merge_remap path (Dict::has_triple_terms gate in parse_ntriples_parallel) which interns triple terms structurally. But the STREAMING external disk-spilling builders (build_external_ntriples_sharded / build_external_ntriples_dictspill in lib.rs) consolidate partial dicts through a hash-SHARDED interner that cannot represent triple terms (a triple term's components are both hash-routed to a shard AND referenced structurally by the triple, breaking the term<->id bijection across shards; intern_parts panics on TermParts::Triple). As of sq-hxgb these paths now call reject_triple_terms_in_external_build to surface a CLEAR error (Graph::build_external) rather than panic/corrupt. The SERIAL external path (sharded=false) already handles them correctly. FIX: give the sharded/dict-spill external build a triple-term-aware consolidation (e.g. a post-pass that re-interns Stored::Triple structurally against the merged dict, or routes triple-term partials to a serial sub-merge) so Graph::build_external accepts reified N-Triples without falling back to in-memory. Referenced in code comments + reject_triple_terms_in_external_build (lib.rs) and test external_build_triple_terms_serial_ok_sharded_errors. Found by Opus 4.8 (sq-hxgb).
close_reason: Closed

title: sparq-py: Term drops base-direction of rdf:dirLangString (query vs query_json diverge)
description:
DISCOVERED during sq-f9tu parity testing. The Python Term API loses the base DIRECTION of an RDF-1.2 directional language string. Through Graph.query, '"x"@en--ltr' and '"x"@en--rtl' are indistinguishable (both: kind=literal, language='en', datatype=rdf:dirLangString). Through Graph.query_json they are correctly distinguished (xml:lang='en--ltr' vs 'en--rtl'). So the two result paths (Term materialisation vs id-level JSON writer) DIVERGE for these literals — a binding-layer fidelity gap.

REPRO: crates/sparq-py/tests/test_parity.py::test_directional_literal_direction_parity_query_vs_json (currently @pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True), bead sq-f9tu). Flip to a hard assert when fixed.

FIX (touches public Term API + skills/python/SKILL.md): either (a) add a base-direction field to Term (e.g. .direction in {'ltr','rtl',None}), populated from oxrdf::Literal direction; or (b) fold direction into .language as the JSON path does (language='en--ltr'). Option (a) is cleaner/typed; (b) matches query_json output exactly. Either way update SKILL.md's Term contract in the same commit.
close_reason: Closed

title: wasm-target clippy: needless_update in sparq-wasm Store::ask_with_max_rows
description: Running 'cargo clippy -p sparq-wasm --all-targets --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings' fails on crates/sparq-wasm/src/lib.rs:274 with clippy::needless_update: 'QueryBudget { max_rows: Some(max_rows), ..Default::default() }'. On wasm32 the QueryBudget struct effectively has only the max_rows field (the wall-clock deadline dimension is native-only; std::time::Instant unusable on wasm32), so the '..Default::default()' struct-update is redundant FOR THE WASM TARGET and clippy flags it. It is fine on native (deadline field present), which is why the native 'cargo clippy --all-targets' gate passes. Pre-existing on main (verified by running the same command on the main worktree) — independent of the sq-9qz6 pt2 wasm test harness. Fix: cfg-gate the struct-update, set the field explicitly, or add #[allow(clippy::needless_update)] on that line. Becomes a hard blocker if/when a wasm-target clippy step is added to CI. [OPUS-4.8]
close_reason: Landed: QueryBudget construction made target-agnostic (unlimited()+field-set); wasm32-target clippy now clean (3 sites incl. tests). Gated (native+wasm clippy clean)+merged.

title: sparq-cli `query` has no result output: only prints solution count (no SELECT rows / --format / ASK boolean / CONSTRUCT triples)
description: The `query` subcommand routes SELECT+ASK+CONSTRUCT through sparq_engine::query and prints only '<n> solutions in <ms>ms' to stdout. Gaps vs the engine's own capabilities + the server's content-negotiation: (1) SELECT does not emit bindings/rows — just a count; (2) no --format / result-format option (the engine has query_json; the server negotiates JSON/XML/CSV/TSV) so the CLI can't emit any SPARQL results serialization; (3) ASK surfaces as '1 solutions'/'0 solutions' instead of a true/false boolean (engine has ask()); (4) CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE exit 1 with 'only SELECT and ASK queries are supported' even though sparq_engine::construct_or_describe exists and bench already routes graph-forms through it. Found while writing crates/sparq-cli/tests/cli_contract.rs (sq-q50l); that test pins the CURRENT behavior so a fix is test-visible. Fix: add result-emitting + --format to cmd_query, mirroring run_query_suite's graph-form routing and the server's negotiate.rs media types.

title: N-Triples loader rejects RDF 1.2 triple-term <<( s p o )>> syntax (write/read asymmetry)
description: sparq-core's fast hand-written N-Triples parser (crates/sparq-core/src/nt.rs parse_chunk / parse_ntriples_parallel) does NOT recognise the N-Triples 1.2 triple-term object syntax <<( s p o )>>. ASYMMETRY: the engine STORES triple terms (Term::Triple), the Turtle loader PARSES <<( )>> fine, and sparq-engine's CONSTRUCT N-Triples serializer (construct::triples_to_ntriples) EMITS <<( )>> via oxrdf Display — but feeding that output back through Graph::load_str(.., "ntriples") fails with 'N-Triples: expected term start' at the <<( . So a CONSTRUCT->serialise->reload round-trip of a graph containing reified statements is lossy for N-Triples (works for Turtle). Repro: load ':r1 rdf:reifies <<( :a :age 30 )>> .' as turtle, construct_ntriples(CONSTRUCT {?s ?p ?o} WHERE {?s ?p ?o}), then Graph::load_str(out, "ntriples") -> Err. FIX: teach nt::parse_chunk (and parse_ntriples_parallel) to parse <<( s p o )>> in object position (N-Triples 1.2 / RDF-star); object-only, may nest. Until fixed, the rdf-star write coverage test crates/sparq-engine/tests/rdfstar_write.rs::ntriples_triple_term_reparse_is_a_known_gap is #[ignore]d and documents the desired behaviour. Found by sq-t267 (Opus 4.8).

title: MPC: semi-honest Shamir has NO tampered-share detection (malicious security gap, guarantee (D))
description: Pinned by sq-nuok adversarial suite (crates/sparq-mpc/src/adversarial_tests.rs, mod tamper). The honest-majority Shamir backend (shamir.rs reconstruct_at_zero / run_secure) performs plain Lagrange interpolation with NO consistency/integrity check. A single corrupted share silently changes the reconstructed secret with no error or signal — even when MAXIMAL redundancy is present (all n shares, of which any t+1 suffice): the impl does not cross-check subsets, so it neither detects nor corrects the inconsistent point. The same holds inside the secure-equality primitive: tampering one share of the opened product m=d·r flips a true MATCH into a non-match (or vice versa) undetected, and inside run_secure's summed sharing (corrupted aggregate). This is CORRECT for the stated semi-honest / honest-but-curious model — malicious security (guarantee (D), active deviation) is explicitly deferred (shamir.rs 'Security model'; backend.rs 'how the trust model stays CONFIGURABLE'). This bead is the durable record of the gap, NOT a request to implement it now. Remediation when malicious-honest-majority is scheduled: verifiable secret sharing (VSS) or information-theoretic MACs behind the SAME MpcBackend trait, reporting malicious_secure=true via BackendInfo. Tests already pin the current (undetected) behaviour so a future fix is observable: the assert_ne! tamper tests would need to become assert(detected-and-errors). NOTE: structural mismatches (wrong evaluation point in a linear op) ARE caught today as a typed Protocol error — only VALUE integrity is unchecked.
design:
MPC tamper-detection design (agent sq-uu0u, 2026-06-14). Maturity: sparq-mpc is honest-majority SEMI-honest; the gap (D) is deliberately-scoped, with absence pinned by passing adversarial_tests.rs::tamper tests.

RECOMMENDATION: Reed–Solomon error-detection/correction (Berlekamp–Welch) over the EXISTING Fp=2^61-1 field. Shamir shares ARE an [n,t+1] RS codeword; with redundancy (n>t+1) detect any tampering and abort; with n>=t+2e+1 correct up to e=floor((n-t-1)/2) cheaters (robust). Zero new deps (no arkworks, no DLOG group), preserves wasm-exclusion. Exploits redundancy currently wasted (tampered_share_with_full_redundancy_is_still_undetected). Matches the already-decided honest-majority v1 trust model.

REJECTED for now (field/scope mismatch): (a) Feldman/Pedersen VSS — needs DLOG group, not Fp; (b) SPDZ IT-MACs — only family for DISHONEST-majority but needs preprocessing + ~2^-61 soundness over Fp = future dishonest-majority backend; (c) Poseidon2/Schnorr share-commitments — right for M4 attestation layer but lives in BN254 Fr (would drag arkworks into lean crate). (b)+(c) = documented future seams, NOT this bead.

THREAT MODEL ACHIEVED: honest-majority, detect-and-abort for any #tampered when n>t+1; robust (guaranteed correct output) for up to e=floor((n-t-1)/2) cheaters. Information-theoretic (no PKI/broadcast/preprocessing).

DOES NOT protect: exactly t+1 shares (no redundancy → no scheme can detect); the degree-2t equality open at n=2t+1 (no RS redundancy there → needs a MAC, deferred); dishonest majority; guarantee (B) end-to-end-to-relying-party and (C) attestation (those are M4 collaborative-proof, gated on RQ1 verifier-soundness remediation).

WORK ITEMS:
- WI-1 (core): RS consistency check + checked/robust reconstruction in shamir.rs (+ maybe robust.rs Berlekamp-Welch). Wire reconstruct/reconstruct_disclosed to use it when redundancy present; preserve exact-t+1 non-detection explicitly. Convert the tamper pins into positive detection tests + property tests.
- WI-2: checked open for the degree-2t equality/mult path (join.rs secure_equal); honestly only detects when n>2t+1; pin the n=2t+1 non-detection boundary. deps WI-1.
- WI-3: surface guarantee via type system — replace BackendInfo::malicious_secure:bool with MaliciousSecurity{None,HonestMajorityAbort,HonestMajorityRobust{max_cheaters}}; update info()+no-fake-crypto tests. deps WI-1,WI-2.
- WI-4 (doc-only): record deferred seams (SPDZ-MAC dishonest-majority backend incl. the n=2t+1 equality gap; Poseidon2/Schnorr share-commitments for M4 attestation) in PLAN.md + as beads.

Gate (all WIs): cargo test -p sparq-mpc (+--release stress), clippy -D warnings, fmt, and cargo tree -p sparq-wasm must still EXCLUDE sparq-mpc.
Key files: shamir.rs:274-299/389-392/306-384, adversarial_tests.rs:61-231, join.rs:399-424, backend.rs:51-96, field.rs:33-145, PLAN.md, research/mpc-zkp-research-and-architecture.md §4.2/5.1/5.3.

title: HDT: PFC block-sequential dict decode + borrowed-slice interning

Each upstream extract(id) re-walks the PFC block from its start (~8 redundant vbyte-delta steps) and allocs a fresh Vec<u8>+String per id, though sparq materializes every id in each section exactly once. Acceptance: dict-decode stage time down, differential BTreeSet equality across block boundaries, reduced alloc count.

SPARQL parsing uses vendored spargebra recursive descent (crates/sparq-engine/src/lib.rs:379); deep nesting is bounded only by --max-body-bytes (1 MiB default), not by an explicit parse-depth constant. SHACL has explicit cycle/recursion guards (sparq-shacl path.rs/eval.rs) but the SPARQL path does not. Risk: a pathological 1 MiB query of deeply nested groups/expressions could deep-recurse the parser (stack). Remediation: add a fuzz assertion / corpus entry for deeply-nested SPARQL (parse_sparql target already exists) confirming no stack overflow at the body cap, OR add an explicit nesting-depth guard. Ref sq-toze / sq-toze.10. [OPUS-4.8]

Optionally bytes-on-disk of a save-produced archive once the in-memory encoder bead sq-ashy lands (until then write goes through temp-NT round-trip -> encode-perf parity is an explicit non-goal). Competitors: hdt-cpp + hdt-java (rdfhdt refs; core LGPL / tools Apache; rdfhdt/hdt-cpp docker exists; rdf2hdt/hdt2rdf/hdtSearch). Fair = load + memory + TP resolution on the same .hdt, matching mapped (mmap) vs loaded (in-RAM) regimes. CRITICAL CAVEAT: sparq-hdt DECODES HDT into sparq's own Dict/Graph (HDT as ingest format) then queries its own indexes; hdt-cpp/java query compressed BitmapTriples in place (HDT as queryable store). So load-and-decode-to-native is the ONLY like-for-like; query-over-HDT head-to-head is NOT — gate/compare load+decode only. Adapter report-cli/docker, behind the hdt cargo feature.

MPC: tighten oblivious shuffle to the AS-Waksman optimal switch count (-1 switch/level)
description: crates/sparq-mpc/src/oblivious.rs builds the plain Benes/Waksman recursive network (floor(m/2) input + floor(m/2) output switches per level). The AS-Waksman redundancy-removal optimization fixes the first output pair (no switch) to shave one switch per recursion level -> ~n fewer conditional swaps overall, the optimal arbitrary-size count ~n*ceil(log2 n)-n+1. We deferred it because the naive fixed-pair pinning over-constrains the routing for ODD m (output 1 pinned BOTTOM clashes with the odd-trailing input pinned TOP); the correct AS-Waksman routing seeds the alternating path so the fixed pair is a consequence, not an axiom. Perf-only: the plain form is already O(n log n) and routes/has-full-support for all permutations (tested to n=9). Verify any change still reaches all n! perms (the anti-Benes-bias property) and routes every permutation (brute-force to n=7). [OPUS-4.8] From sq-18lk.

title: sparq-core: chunk-parallel TriG IN-MEMORY loader (reuse turtle_chunks statement chunking)
description: load_dataset routes TriG to the SERIAL oxttl path (load_dataset_serial); only N-Quads got the chunk-parallel + sharded-merge fast path in sq-25r3 (PR feat-parallel-nquads-loader). TriG is the deferred half: it is NOT line-oriented (it nests GRAPH g { ... } / { ... } blocks carrying Turtle's @prefix/@base scope and document-scoped blank-node labels), so byte-range newline chunking is wrong. The tractable approach is to reuse the existing turtle_chunks statement-terminator chunking (prefix-snapshot broadcast + interspersed-directive replay) extended to (a) track the enclosing GRAPH block as routing context per statement and (b) handle the block-open/close + the 'g {' / 'GRAPH g {' headers as units, then run the per-graph sharded-dict merge already factored out as merge_partials(). Gate on the parallel feature, keep the serial fallback, and add a differential test (chunked == load_dataset_serial, byte-identical: default + named graphs, bnodes across chunks, multiple/blank-node-named graphs) mirroring parallel_nquads_matches_serial. Distinct from the out-of-core quad build. Risk: blank-node + prefix scope across GRAPH blocks and chunk boundaries — correctness is paramount, fall back to serial on any mis-split.

title: MPC: multi-secret / batched share_private_input (per-row hidden values, vectors, per-graph commitments)

Generalise to batched/vector secret sharing (Vec<Fp> per holder with a documented row-binding) so the secure aggregate and hidden-value join can range over more than one value per source. Prerequisite to any realistic multi-row hidden federated query. Gap raised in the area but not in its proposed-bead list; surfaced here so it is not lost.
