title: MPC: federation-level OWA / omission negative tests (a dropped holder/graph/credential must not forge a valid result)
description: Architecture conventions #8 and §4.2 require endpoint-independent OWA-safe semantics: omitting credentials must not forge a valid result, and a short-count/dropped-graph view must be detectable (the issuer-signed true-triple-count + salt in §4.3 step 1 is the intended defence). The crate has holder-level and join-soundness tests but NO federation-level negative test that a holder dropping a graph, returning a truncated partial, or omitting a contributor either cannot fabricate a passing result or is surfaced as a detectable discrepancy. These tests also document honestly which omissions are NOT yet detectable pre-M4 (no signed count binding yet). Acceptance: dropped-holder / truncated-partial / omitted-row negative tests each asserting the actual behaviour.

title: MPC: oblivious hidden-value join must hide the bipartite MATCH STRUCTURE, not just the payload multiset (privacy spike, distinct from the perf bead)
description: HiddenValueJoin opens m=d*r for every (i,j) pair, so whoever drives the opens learns the full bipartite match pattern (which left row matched which right row), even though the output multiset is canonicalised. True circuit-PSI/oblivious join reveals only the match COUNT or the joined multiset, never positional structure. This is a PRIVACY property orthogonal to the O(|L|*|R|) PERF concern already filed (sq-t21/sq-h99, both confirmed DEFERRED): the cuckoo-bin opt could be built without fixing the positional leak and vice versa. Spike: characterise exactly what the all-pairs open leaks to each party, state it in the join doc, scope the oblivious-shuffle/shuffled-open mitigation, and pin the current leakage with a test before any fix.

title: MPC: collision-resistant Term->Fp key encoding + injectivity contract for HiddenValueJoin
description: HiddenValueJoin takes the private join key as a pre-encoded Fp and the struct doc admits the encoding is the holder's untested responsibility (tests use a hand-injective small-int map). For real RDF Terms, secret-shared field equality is a SOUND stand-in for term equality only if the encoding is injective on the join domain (a collision = a false match = a soundness break the differential tests can't see because they avoid collisions by construction). Provide a documented Term->Fp encoder (domain-separated hash into Fp, stating the 2^61-1 birthday bound) + a collision-detection path or explicit assumption + near-collision test. The on-ramp the M4 in-circuit encoding-correctness proof will later constrain.

title: ZK: extend filter coverage — negative xsd:integer + xsd:decimal + general xsd:double (currently fail-closed/unprovable)
description: filter_int.nr handles only canonical non-negative integers (D<=19, no sign); negative integers, xsd:decimal, and the general fractional/scientific/rounded double fragment are all rejected fail-closed. Sound but narrow — bounds which real credential FILTER queries can be proven (negative coordinates, decimal amounts). Add a signed-integer + a decimal/IEEE-parse circuit member with an in-circuit decimal->IEEE round-to-nearest-even path; measure gates with `bb gates` first per noir-optimisation.

title: ZK: bind HolderPoP to a SPECIFIC credential (issuer-attested holder<->credential binding)
description: bind_holder_pop proves possession of a holder key trusted by an external registry but NOT that the key is bound to the presented credential (README/verifier doc: deferred). A trusted holder can therefore present a credential issued to a DIFFERENT holder. Have the issuer attest a holder-key binding (extend sparq_zk::sig signed object) and the verifier require the PoP key match the credential's attested holder, closing the sender-constraint gap.

title: ZK: in-circuit entailment-closure proof — prove an UNDISCLOSED antecedent is in the committed graph's RDFS/OWL closure
description: sq-314 enforces derivation_steps but only grounds them over the DISCLOSED base (verifier.rs doc 'deferred: in-circuit closure proof'). So an entailed claim must disclose every antecedent, defeating privacy for inference-bearing presentations (the §5 inference goal). Add a derivation_step circuit proving a derived triple's antecedent occurs in a committed graph's RDFS-rule closure without disclosing it, bound to the scan commitments — the privacy upgrade for the Rdfs/Owl regimes.

title: sparq-hdt: direct in-memory PFC + BitmapTriples encoder for HDT write (skip the temp N-Triples round-trip)
description: write.rs save() materializes the whole graph as N-Triples text on disk then has hdt::Hdt::read_nt re-parse+re-intern it — work sparq already did on ingest, plus a full-graph text spill. The fast path is a direct FourSectDict (PFC) + BitmapTriples (SPO) encoder fed from sparq's id space — the exact inverse of decode.rs, which already exists and is differentially tested. Upstream-blocked on a missing builder API (UPSTREAM.md sq-2te path B), so roll-your-own per the repo's upstream-blocker policy. Larger unit; gate on round-trip byte/term-set equality + hdt-cpp interop.
close_reason: Closed

title: ZK: sparse/compressed key-set inclusion for the hidden_issuer circuit (dense 2^D host builder bounds issuer registry size)
description: issuer::key_set_root is a DENSE 2^D-leaf host builder and only hidden_issuer_d4 (16 keys) is compiled — the identical O(2^depth) limitation sq-hwe (confirmed OPEN) is fixing for the revoke status-list circuit, but on a DIFFERENT circuit and uncovered by any bead (sq-hwe/sq-6qe are status-list-scoped). A large/growing issuer registry has no path. The key_set_membership relation is depth-generic; needs a sparse builder + a larger compiled member, mirroring the sq-hwe approach — sequence to reuse that design.

title: sparq-core: stream (or sparse-build) numerics/temporals caches on the in-RAM build/save finalize
description: The in-RAM build/save path (lib.rs:1002-1007) allocates DENSE numerics_of (8 B/term) + temporals_of (16 B/term) over every distinct term at finalize — an O(distinct-terms) RSS spike on top of the dict. The dict-spill path already STREAM-writes these (dictspill.rs:883-953); the in-memory save path does not. Apply the same streaming write to save()/save_compressed(), and/or build the temporals cache sparse-from-the-start. Measurably trims the finalize RSS peak research/wikidata-lowresource-stage1.md flags.

title: sparq-core: write compressed SPQCPRM1 perms directly from build_external (skip the recompress second pass)
description: build_external writes raw [u32;3] perms; producing the 2.5-2.75x-smaller SPQCPRM1 format (compressed-perms-verdict.md) today requires a SEPARATE full-index recompress pass. Fold the FoR+varint block encoder into the existing sibling-sort spill/merge tail so the build emits compressed perms in one pass when requested (env/flag gated, raw stays the default per the verdict). Saves a full second pass over an 84+ GB index at 1B scale. Gate: byte-identity vs build-then-recompress + open/query parity.

title: Build release artifacts with cargo-auditable so the dependency list ships inside the binary
description: The CycloneDX SBOM is a separate artifact; the shipped sparq-cli/sparq-server binaries carry no embedded dep manifest, so an operator can't run `cargo audit bin sparq-server` post-incident. title: MPC: equality/mult open only DETECTS, never CORRECTS, under the honest-majority party count
description: Discovered during WI-2 (sq-7q9i). The degree-2t equality/mult open now routes through the RS checker (reconstruct_degree -> reconstruct_robust at degree 2t), but the honest-majority constructor fixes t=floor((n-1)/2), so for a degree-2t product: odd n gives n=2t+1 (ZERO redundancy -> no detection, needs a MAC = WI-4/sq-6d6g); even n gives exactly one redundant share (e_max = floor((n-2t-1)/2) = 0 -> DETECT-and-abort only). Robust CORRECTION at degree 2t (e_max>=1) needs n>=2t+3, which the constructor NEVER provisions for the equality primitive. So in practice secure_equal can at best detect-and-abort (even n), never auto-correct a cheater. The reconstruct_degree correction arm IS exercised by a property test that builds a degree-2t sharing directly with n>=2t+3, but no production path reaches it. Follow-up options: (a) allow the equality test to open its degree-2t product over an OVER-PROVISIONED party set (n>=2t+3) when robustness (not just abort) is wanted; (b) reduce the product degree back to t via a BGW/DN degree-reduction round before opening, so the open is degree-t with the full degree-t correction budget; (c) leave detect-and-abort as the honest envelope and document it. Decide + implement/document. Files: crates/sparq-mpc/src/shamir.rs (reconstruct_degree doc), join.rs (secure_equal), adversarial_tests.rs (degree_2t_open_* props).

title: Migrate to sha2 0.11 (Dependabot PR #17) — major API bump needs code changes
description: Dependabot PR #17 bumps sha2 0.10.9->0.11.0 (RustCrypto traits 0.11). Fails build/clippy — needs code migration (Digest API). Do the migration on a branch incl. the bump; Dependabot PR auto-closes on merge. Sibling: sq-8bhq (quick-xml 0.40).
notes:
INVESTIGATED (deps-major-migrations branch, [OPUS-4.8]). Status: production sha2 0.11 migration ALREADY DONE on main (commit 561fae7) — sparq-engine uses sha2/sha1/md-5 = "0.11" with digest 0.11; the SPARQL hash builtins (MD5/SHA1/SHA256/SHA384/SHA512 via digest_hex<D: md5::Digest>) compile + pass under 0.11. The ONLY thing Dependabot PR #17 changes is sparq-zk dev-dependency sha2 = "0.10" -> "0.11" (crates/sparq-zk/Cargo.toml). That bump is BLOCKED-UPSTREAM and INFEASIBLE without vendoring rdf-canon: rdf-canon 0.15.3 (LATEST published; confirmed via sparse index — no 0.16+, no digest-0.11 release) takes a digest::Digest (digest 0.10) generic bound on canonicalize_quads_with::<D>/issue_quads_with::<D>. The dev-only test crates/sparq-zk/tests/rdf_canon_suite.rs:117/131 feeds sha2::Sha384 straight into it for the W3C rdf-canon test075 SHA-384 parameterized-hash cases. Bumping sparq-zk sha2 to 0.11 makes sha2::Sha384 (digest 0.11) fail the digest-0.10 bound — VERIFIED hard compile error: "the trait bound `Sha384: digest::digest::Digest` is not satisfied ... multiple different versions of crate `digest` in the dependency graph". Note: sha2 0.10.9 ALSO stays in the lockfile transitively via oxrdf 0.3.3 (sha2="0.10") regardless, so 0.10 cannot leave the tree until oxrdf bumps too. DECISION: keep the sparq-zk pin (already carries an [OPUS-4.8] rationale comment); vendoring a full RDFC-1.0 impl to update one dev-dep test is grossly disproportionate. KEEP BEAD OPEN; lift only when rdf-canon publishes a digest-0.11 release (then bump sparq-zk sha2 to 0.11 + drop the pin comment). PR #17 cannot be made green as-is.
sha2 0.11 bump BLOCKED upstream: a dev-dependency (rdf-canon 0.15.3) transitively pins digest 0.10, so the lockfile can't unify on sha2 0.11. Production code is 0.11-ready. Unblocks when rdf-canon bumps to digest 0.11. Dependabot PR #17 closed (can't merge).

title: sparq-solid: precise variable-GRAPH write check under USING/WITH (currently conservative fallback)

Options: (a) expose a pub build_using/active-dataset helper from sparq-engine; (b) translate the QueryDataset into an explicit FROM NAMED list of the kept store named graphs before serializing. title: sparq-solid: precise per-solution write check for variable GRAPH ?var update targets
description: PodStore::update_as (sq-xor3) currently treats a DELETE/INSERT...WHERE template with a variable GRAPH ?var slot conservatively: it requires the actor to hold write on EVERY graph in the store, denying otherwise. This is sound (fail-closed) but over-restrictive — a precise check would evaluate the WHERE pattern, instantiate the template graph slots per solution (the engine already does this in instantiate_templates), and check only the ACTUAL target graphs against the write grants. Needs care: the per-solution targets must be checked before the in-place apply, so either pre-evaluate (cost) or push the check into the engine's update path behind a hook. Same conservative handling applies to CLEAR/DROP ALL|NAMED (acceptable for those — they genuinely span all graphs). Source: crates/sparq-solid/src/update.rs (raise_wildcard on GraphNamePattern::Variable), design doc §4.4.
close_reason: Landed: per-solution write check for variable GRAPH ?var (evaluates bindings against the authorized view, fail-closed fallback). Gated+merged.

title: mmap dict: quoted-triple component id that is in-range but resolves to wrong term kind panics via reconstruct_triple unreachable!
description: Discovered while fixing sq-znld/sq-ed2i/sq-ky2a (branch sec-core-mmap). Dict::open_mmap validate() (crates/sparq-core/src/dict.rs) now range-checks that a StoredRef::Triple component id is 0<c, and (c<INLINE_BASE => c<=len) — preventing OOB. But a component id that IS in range can still point at the WRONG term KIND (e.g. a literal where reconstruct_triple expects an IRI/blank subject or IRI predicate), which hits the unreachable!() in reconstruct_triple (dict.rs ~line 346-351) -> a clean panic (DoS), not UB/OOB. Not reachable by the current mmap_corruption_oracle corpus (the sample graph has no quoted-triple terms, so byte-flips don't synthesise tag-3 records with cross-referencing component ids). Lower severity than sq-znld (panic/DoS, not UB). FIX: reconstruct_triple should return a safe placeholder (like OOR_TERM) instead of unreachable! when a component resolves to an unexpected kind; or open_mmap validate() should topologically verify component kinds. Extend the oracle corpus with a graph containing RDF-star quoted triples to drive this out. Threat-model boundary B5 / T-MMAP-UB neighbourhood. [OPUS-4.8]
close_reason: Landed: reconstruct_triple fails closed (clean error/placeholder, no unreachable! panic) on wrong-kind/cyclic quoted-triple component ids from a tampered index. Oracle extended. Gated+merged.

title: Geo: 1-D set operations (line-line / line-polygon difference, symDifference, intersection) via i_overlay string-line noding
description: ROLL-YOUR-OWN-NOW (was: GeoError::Unsupported in crates/sparq-geo/src/geof.rs). geof:difference / symDifference / intersection over 1-D operands (line-line, line-polygon) currently return GeoError::Unsupported('no linear-referencing subtraction in geo') — see difference_geometry (geof.rs ~809-833), sym_difference_geometry (~852-887), and the LINESTRING x LINESTRING case in intersection. UPSTREAM DEP: the geo crate (georust/geo 0.33) BooleanOps only nodes/overlays POLYGONS; it provides no linear-referencing subtraction for open paths. ROLL-YOUR-OWN PLAN: geo's BooleanOps is backed by i_overlay (already in Cargo.lock at 4.5.2 via geo 0.33). i_overlay exposes a string-line / open-path overlay API (StringGraph / overlay of line strings with Subject/Clip + OverlayRule) that DOES segment-node 1-D inputs. Implement line set-ops by lowering our LineString operands to i_float IntPoint paths, running i_overlay's string overlay with the appropriate OverlayRule (Difference / Xor / Intersect), and lifting results back to geo_types LineString/MultiLineString — gated by the differential vs a reference (e.g. JTS/shapely via the geo conformance harness sq-9h1r). This unblocks the per-row expression errors documented in crates/sparq-geo/README.md set-ops table. UPSTREAM ISSUE/PR: file georust/geo feature request 'BooleanOps / linear-referencing difference for LineString operands' (https://github.com/georust/geo) referencing i_overlay's string-line support; offer to contribute the geo-side adapter. Found by upstream-blocker sweep (sq-mig0, Opus 4.8).
close_reason: Landed: 1-D line set-ops (line-line/line-polygon difference+symDiff) via rolled-own + i_overlay; exact partition verified. Upstream issue -> sq-ykzi. Gated+merged.

title: External (sharded/dict-spill) N-Triples build does not support RDF 1.2 triple terms
description: The disk-spilling external N-Triples builders (build_external_ntriples_sharded via ShardedDict::intern_partials, and build_external_ntriples_dictspill via SpillInterner::intern_batch) consolidate partial dicts through a HASH-SHARDED interner that cannot represent RDF 1.2 triple terms (<<( s p o )>>): a triple term's components are hash-routed to a shard AND referenced structurally by the triple, breaking the term<->id bijection across shards (the in-shard interners assert/panic on Term::Triple). sq-hxgb taught the byte parser (nt::parse_chunk) to ACCEPT triple-term objects, and the IN-MEMORY parallel loader (parse_ntriples_parallel) now falls back to the serial merge_remap when any partial contains one. The SERIAL external path (build_external_ntriples_parallel / merge_remap, sharded=false) also handles them. But the SHARDED and DICT-SPILL external paths now return a CLEAR ERROR (reject_triple_terms_in_external_build in lib.rs) instead of panicking/corrupting. FIX: give the sharded/spill consolidation a real triple-term path (e.g. route triple-term components to their shards first, then intern the triple referencing the resolved shard ids in a second pass; or fall the affected batch back to serial merge). Until then, Graph::build_external on triple-term N-Triples must use the serial path (SPARQ_SHARDED_DICT=0) or load in memory. Found by sq-hxgb (Opus 4.8).

title: sparq-core parse_to_triples silently parses unknown format strings as Turtle (catch-all _ => Turtle)
description: Graph::parse_to_triples (crates/sparq-core/src/lib.rs ~635) matches known format strings (ntriples/nquads/trig) and uses a catch-all '_ => Turtle' arm for EVERYTHING else, including typos and unsupported formats. So Graph::load_str(text, "bogusfmt") silently parses as Turtle and returns Ok instead of erroring. The sparq-cli workaround (is_known_format guard in load_quiet + cmd_build, added under sq-q50l) catches it at the CLI boundary, but other callers (sparq-server graph-store ingest, load_dataset, build_external) inherit the silent fallback. Consider an explicit Turtle alias set (turtle|ttl|text/turtle|application/turtle) + an Err for unknown formats — but audit blast radius first: many call sites pass a literal "turtle" that currently hits the catch-all and must keep working. Discovered while writing crates/sparq-cli/tests/cli_contract.rs.

title: update_in_place is non-atomic on multi-op request failure (no engine-level rollback)
description: FINDING (sq-qu8o, contract tests in crates/sparq-engine/src/update.rs mod update_contract): a SPARQL UPDATE *request* is a ;-separated op sequence and per SPARQL 1.1 should be all-or-nothing, but the engine's delta-overlay entry point update_in_place(&mut Graph, sparql) applies ops in place and, on op K failing, leaves ops 0..K-1 committed (a partial prefix) — verified by test in_place_request_is_partial_on_error_by_contract. This is currently DOCUMENTED-and-relied-upon (sparq_serve::ApplyUpdates::apply contract; the serve writer recovers atomicity via fork -> apply -> seal-only-on-Ok), so the PRODUCTION HTTP path IS request-atomic. The rebuild path update() is atomic by construction (rebuild_request_is_atomic). The gap: any direct library consumer of update_in_place gets silent partial application on error — a footgun. Options: (a) add an atomic update_in_place wrapper (fork+seal internally) as the public default; (b) document the non-atomicity on update_in_place's rustdoc + steer callers to update() or the fork pattern; (c) leave as-is (serve is the only first-party caller). Low priority: no production-path bug, fully test-pinned. NOT a SILENT-contract bug — CLEAR/DROP/CREATE auto-create no-op success is spec-conformant (SHOULD, not MUST, conditioned on recording empty graphs).

title: Core: cheap O(overlay) Graph::snapshot API (Arc-shared immutable base)
description: Add a cheap Graph snapshot that shares the immutable base (perms + compacted dict arena) behind Arcs so snapshots are O(overlay), not O(triples). Unblocks the server double-buffer collapse, Python Graph.copy(), and the RSP overlay-snapshot EvalMode. Structural change across every storage mode (incl. mmap + compressed). Design in the design field. (was the workspace TODO.md cheap-snapshot rationale — now beaded + doc deleted)
design:
Cheap O(overlay) Graph snapshot API — the core structural change that unblocks the
server double-buffer collapse (sq-dfs), Python Graph.copy() (sq-6h8), and the RSP
overlay-snapshot EvalMode (sq-j39). (Design preserved from the deleted workspace TODO.md.)

PROBLEM. `Graph` is not (and should not be naively) `Clone`: a deep copy of the
dictionary arena and the six permutation indexes is O(n). The server's SPARQL Update
path (crates/sparq-server/src/http.rs::Writer) currently gets microsecond steady-state
updates WITHOUT core changes by double-buffering — two physical Graphs alternate between
*published* and *spare* — but that pays ~2x graph residency, a one-time O(graph) rebuild
on the first update (and again after a failed update discards a buffer), and a
spare-reclaim wait/rebuild when a reader holds a snapshot past the query budget.

PROPOSED API.
  - `Graph::snapshot(&self) -> GraphSnapshot` (or make `Graph` a cheap `Clone`): an O(1)
    copy that SHARES the immutable base — `TripleStore::perms` and the compacted dictionary
    storage behind `Arc`s — with the mutable parts (the delta `Overlay`, the append-only
    dictionary tail, the numeric-cache tail) either cloned (small, O(pending updates)) or
    made copy-on-write.
  - The server then keeps ONE master `Graph`, `update_in_place`s it (µs), and publishes
    `Arc::new(master.snapshot())` per commit. The publish slot stays
    `RwLock<Arc<Graph>>` + single-writer mutex; only the Writer's buffer juggling collapses.

REQUIREMENTS the API must meet:
  1. Snapshots are O(overlay), NEVER O(triples).
  2. Immutable and `Send + Sync`.
  3. Unaffected by later `update_in_place`/`compact` on the master — compaction must not
     invalidate live snapshots (the new base goes into FRESH `Arc`s).

COST / why it is structural (not an additive seam): meeting (1)–(3) means moving
`TripleStore`'s permutation storage and the dictionary's compacted arena behind `Arc`s — a
change to EVERY storage mode, including mmap + compressed. This is why sq-dfs / sq-6h8 /
sq-j39 are all blocked on it.

WINS over the current server double-buffer: removes the ~2x graph residency; removes the
one-time O(graph) rebuild the first update pays to materialise the second buffer (and the
re-pay after a failed update); removes the spare-reclaim wait/rebuild fallback when a
reader holds a snapshot past the query budget.

The salt is a per-graph RDFC10 bnode nonce (audit #9), not the issuer identity, so disclosing it does NOT reveal WHICH issuer signed — but it is a per-graph value disclosed in the clear and participates in the audit-#9 salt-uniqueness check. title: HDT: bump hdt 0.4 -> 0.6 once qwt prefetch nightly requirement is gone
description: hdt crate version pin — KEPT: pinned to hdt = 0.4 (not 0.6) because hdt 0.6.0 -> qwt 0.3.4 default 'prefetch' feature requires nightly on aarch64. Bump when qwt drops/feature-gates that or hdt disables the feature.  (was a markdown TODO: crates/sparq-hdt/TODO.md:44 — now beaded + to be stripped from the doc)
notes: [upstream-sweep sq-mig0, Opus 4.8] ROLL-YOUR-OWN PATH (not a dead-end wait). UPSTREAM DEP: hdt 0.6 -> qwt 0.3.4 whose DEFAULT 'prefetch' feature uses core::intrinsics::prefetch_read_data (nightly-only on aarch64). qwt is NOT currently in our Cargo.lock (we pin hdt 0.4 which has no qwt). PLAN: bump hdt to 0.6 with default-features=false and add a [patch.crates-io] entry pointing qwt at a vendored fork (vendor/qwt) that feature-GATES the prefetch intrinsic behind a non-default 'prefetch' feature (or replaces it with a stable no-op / _mm_prefetch on x86) — i.e. the same vendor-local pattern AGENTS.md prescribes (as done for spargebra). Then enable hdt 0.6 on STABLE aarch64. NOTE: per research/parsing-optimization-plan.md, hdt 0.6 also builds *more* unused query structure (a qwt wavelet) that our decode.rs already bypasses — so the upgrade's only payoff is staying current, not perf; weigh accordingly (P4 is correct). UPSTREAM ISSUE/PR: file rossanoventurini/qwt (https://github.com/rossanoventurini/qwt) to feature-gate the nightly prefetch intrinsic (make 'prefetch' opt-in or stable-fallback); secondary: KonradHoeffner/hdt to expose qwt feature flags. Tractability: MEDIUM (small qwt patch).

title: HDT: upstream decode-only entry point to skip pattern indexes on ingest
description: Loader gaps (upstream API shape) — DEFERRED: Hdt::read eagerly builds its own object-position index (and in 0.6 a wavelet matrix) for pattern queries we never run — pure ingest could skip it. An upstream 'decode only' entry point would cut HDT->Graph load time.  (was a markdown TODO: crates/sparq-hdt/TODO.md:55 — now beaded + to be stripped from the doc)
notes: [upstream-sweep sq-mig0, Opus 4.8] LARGELY DONE / NOW UNBLOCKABLE — we already rolled our own decode-only path. EVIDENCE: crates/sparq-hdt/src/decode.rs is a sparq-side direct SPO decoder (graph_from_reader, the DEFAULT load path — lib.rs:171) that reads bitmap_y/z + sequence_y/z + PFC sections directly and SKIPS upstream TriplesBitmap::new (wavelet matrix, OP-index, per-object Vec<Vec<u32>>) — exactly the 'skip pattern indexes on ingest' this bead asked upstream for. The slow upstream path is retained only as the differential oracle (load_reader_via_upstream, lib.rs:178). REMAINING work is just the UPSTREAM contribution: file KonradHoeffner/hdt (https://github.com/KonradHoeffner/hdt) proposing a 'decode-only' / streaming-triples entry point on Hdt (read the dict + bitmaps, yield (s,p,o) without building TriplesBitmap query structures), citing our decode.rs as a reference impl; if accepted we can drop our vendored decoder for the upstream one. Tractability of the remaining (upstream PR): MEDIUM. The local feature is effectively shipped — this bead can be reframed from 'blocked' to 'contribute upstream'.

title: HDT: write support (Graph -> .hdt) when upstream gains in-memory builder
description: Write support — DEFERRED (blocked-upstream): hdt 0.6.0 has no in-memory triples -> FourSectDict builder API, so Graph -> .hdt would mean serializing to a temp N-Triples file first. Revisit when upstream grows an in-memory builder.  (was a markdown TODO: crates/sparq-hdt/TODO.md:34 — now beaded + to be stripped from the doc)
notes: [upstream-sweep sq-mig0, Opus 4.8] NOW UNBLOCKABLE — the 'blocked-upstream / no in-memory builder' framing is OUTDATED. EVIDENCE: the wrapped hdt crate (KonradHoeffner/hdt) DOES expose a builder: Hdt::read_nt(path) builds a full archive from N-Triples and Hdt::write(&mut w) serialises it — already used in crates/sparq-hdt/tests/roundtrip.rs:73, examples/bench_load.rs:100-102, examples/bench_direct_vs_upstream.rs:97-99 (behind the crate's 'sophia' dev-dep feature). Also FourSectDict / DictSectPFC are pub and already used by our decode.rs. TWO roll-your-own paths: (A) cheap NOW: Graph -> serialize to N-Triples (we already serialize NT) -> hdt::Hdt::read_nt -> hdt.write(file); add an opt-in 'write' feature that pulls hdt's 'sophia' feature for the writer; gate by a round-trip differential (write then load == original BTreeSet). (B) faster, optional: vendor a direct in-memory FourSectDict + BitmapTriples builder (mirror of our decode.rs in reverse) so we skip the NT text round-trip. UPSTREAM ISSUE/PR: file KonradHoeffner/hdt (https://github.com/KonradHoeffner/hdt) requesting a feature-gate so read_nt/write are available WITHOUT the heavy sophia adapter (an in-memory builder entry point taking an iterator of (s,p,o) id/string triples) — and offer the PR. Tractability: path (A) LOW/EASY; path (B) MEDIUM.
close_reason: Landed: opt-in sparq_hdt::save (feature 'write') via temp-NT round-trip; 7 tests incl. upstream-oracle conformance; honest about cost; in-memory-builder path -> sq-0enu + upstream PR drafted. Gated+merged.
